questions.explanation: "The winner will receive a laptop." The set of books goes to "everyone on the shortlist", not only the winner.

questions.question: Winners will be told the results by ____ in May.
questions.explanation: "We won’t be sending emails … Instead, the winners will be contacted by phone in the middle of May".

questions.question: Why did Aisha start her business?
options: a) She felt bad about wasted clothes.
b) She saw a chance to make a lot of money.
c) Her flatmates asked her to help them.
questions.explanation: The clothing they threw away "shocked me" and "I felt quite ashamed. That’s really what got me started." Money was not the reason: "Making money didn’t come into it at first."

questions.question: What was most difficult for Aisha at the beginning?
options: a) Learning how to sew well enough
b) Finding enough old jeans to work with
c) Getting shops to sell what she made
questions.explanation: "The hard part was persuading shops to stock our products." Sewing was easy for her: "The sewing wasn’t a problem. My grandmother taught me".

questions.question: How does Aisha feel about being a boss now?
options: a) She still prefers to check all the work herself.
b) She is happy to let her team make decisions.
c) She would rather go back to working alone.
questions.explanation: "Now I trust the team to make their own decisions". Checking everything herself was what she did "at first", and she says "I love it", so she does not want to work alone.

questions.question: What is Aisha’s opinion about the price of her bags?
options: a) It is fair because of how they are made.
b) It should be lower so more people can buy them.
c) It is the reason why some shops refuse them.
questions.explanation: They are "made by hand" and "we pay our staff properly", so "if you want something made fairly, it’s going to cost a bit more." She does not want to lower the price, and shops refused her products because they "looked cheap", not because of the price.

questions.question: What does Aisha think is the most important thing her business does?
options: a) It gives jobs to young people in Leeds.
b) It stops tonnes of denim being thrown away.
c) It changes the way people see old things.
questions.explanation: Customers "start looking at their own clothes differently, and that matters more than the tonnes we collect." So the denim saved is less important to her.

questions.question: What does Aisha want to do in the future?
options: a) Sell her products in other countries
b) Teach children to mend clothes
c) Open a large factory near Leeds
questions.explanation: "What I would like is to run workshops in schools, so that children can learn to repair their own clothes." She is "not interested" in a big factory.

questions.question: What does the notice say?
options: a) Group B’s lessons will start at a different time.
b) Group B will study in a different room this week.
c) Group B will have a new teacher for this week.
questions.explanation: The notice says "this week’s classes will be in Room 4" instead of Room 12. It also says "Your teacher and lesson times stay the same", so neither the teacher nor the time changes.

questions.question: What should students who want to go on the trip do?
options: a) Pay the coach driver on Friday morning.
b) Arrive at 8.15 to get their ticket.
c) Buy a ticket at reception using a card.
questions.explanation: Tickets are "on sale at reception" and "Payment is by card only". Nobody pays on the coach, and 8.15 is the time the coach "leaves", so it is too late to buy a ticket then.

questions.question: What does Kenji want to do?
options: a) Have the exchange on a different day
b) Stop doing the conversation exchange
c) Meet somewhere other than the library café
questions.explanation: Kenji asks "Could we do tomorrow at the same time instead?", so he wants to move the exchange to another day. He says "Same place, the library café", and he only cancels today’s meeting, not the whole exchange.

questions.question: What does the notice say about the laptops?
options: a) Students may only use them inside the centre.
b) Students can take them home if they show their card.
c) Students can keep them for 15 minutes at a time.
questions.explanation: Laptops are "for use in this room only", so they cannot leave the centre. The student card is shown "at the desk" to borrow one, not to take it home, and the 15 minutes refers to returning laptops "before the centre closes", not to how long you can use one.

questions.question: What does Ms Okafor tell the students?
options: a) The writing test will take place on Monday.
b) The test room will be announced on Monday.
c) They should bring a dictionary to the test.
questions.explanation: She asks students to "check the noticeboard on Monday to find out which room you are in". The test itself is "next Wednesday", and dictionaries are not allowed: "You will not be allowed to use dictionaries".

questions.question: Callum is a university student who loves classical music. He needs a cheap ticket, and he must leave by nine o’clock to catch the last bus home.
options: A) Symphony under the Stars
B) Blue Note Supper Club
C) The Snow Queen
D) City Chamber Orchestra
E) Behind the Curtain
F) The Cellar Sessions
G) Jungle Beats
H) Laugh Out Loud
questions.explanation: The City Chamber Orchestra plays "Mozart and Haydn", the concert "finishes at about 8.45" and "students pay half price". Symphony under the Stars is also classical, but it "starts at 9 pm" and "there are no reduced prices for children or students".

questions.question: Sophie wants to take her six-year-old daughter to a show on Saturday afternoon. Her daughter is very active and would enjoy a show where she can take part rather than just sit and watch.
options: A) Symphony under the Stars
B) Blue Note Supper Club
C) The Snow Queen
D) City Chamber Orchestra
E) Behind the Curtain
F) The Cellar Sessions
G) Jungle Beats
H) Laugh Out Loud
questions.explanation: Jungle Beats is for "children aged three to eight", has a show on "Saturday and Sunday at 2 pm", and children "are invited onto the stage to play drums" and dance. The Snow Queen has an afternoon show for children, but "The audience is asked to stay in their seats throughout".

questions.question: Tariq is taking his parents out for their wedding anniversary. They all love jazz and would like to have dinner while they listen to the music.
options: A) Symphony under the Stars
B) Blue Note Supper Club
C) The Snow Queen
D) City Chamber Orchestra
E) Behind the Curtain
F) The Cellar Sessions
G) Jungle Beats
H) Laugh Out Loud
questions.explanation: At the Blue Note Supper Club you "Enjoy a three-course dinner while the Ruth Adebayo Quartet plays jazz favourites", and it is "perfect for celebrations". The Cellar Sessions also has jazz, but "The bar serves drinks but no food".

questions.question: Hannah and her friends want to see something that will make them laugh. They can only go out on Monday evenings, and they don’t want to pay more than £10 each.
options: A) Symphony under the Stars
B) Blue Note Supper Club
C) The Snow Queen
D) City Chamber Orchestra
E) Behind the Curtain
F) The Cellar Sessions
G) Jungle Beats
H) Laugh Out Loud
questions.explanation: Laugh Out Loud has comedians "every Monday night" and "Tickets are just £8". Behind the Curtain is also a "clever comedy", but it runs "from Tuesday to Saturday" and tickets "cost £18".

questions.question: Laura is a drama student. She wants to see a new play by a modern writer, and she’d love the chance to ask the actors questions about their work.
options: A) Symphony under the Stars
B) Blue Note Supper Club
C) The Snow Queen
D) City Chamber Orchestra
E) Behind the Curtain
F) The Cellar Sessions
G) Jungle Beats
H) Laugh Out Loud
questions.explanation: Behind the Curtain was "written last year by local writer Joe Kirwan", and on Thursday "the cast will stay on stage to answer questions from the audience". At The Snow Queen the puppeteers also "answer questions", but it is a "classic story" told with puppets, not a new play.

questions.question: How did Isla begin going to ballet classes?
options: a) Her school offered free lessons on Saturdays.
b) A teacher saw her outside the class.
c) Her mother booked lessons for her sixth birthday.
d) She asked her sister if she could join her class.
questions.explanation: Isla watched "through the window" and then "the teacher noticed me and invited me in." Her sister was already in the class, but Isla never asked to join; the teacher invited her.

questions.question: What does Isla say about ballet?
options: a) She has always liked it more than other styles.
b) She stopped doing it when she found contemporary dance.
c) She still finds all its rules boring.
d) Contemporary dance showed her why it was useful.
questions.explanation: After trying contemporary dance, "Suddenly I understood the point of ballet. It gives you strength and control." She did not always like it ("I found it quite boring as a child"), and she did not stop: "Now I do both styles."

questions.question: How does Isla feel now about missing evenings with her friends?
options: a) She has learned to accept the situation.
b) She worries that they will stop being her friends.
c) She is still upset when they go out without her.
d) She wants to train less so she can join them.
questions.explanation: Isla says: "That used to upset me, but now I accept it." She was upset in the past, not now, and her friends "come to all my shows", so she is not worried about losing them.

questions.question: What does Isla say about her ankle injury?
options: a) It still hurts when she does some movements.
b) It was the reason she tried contemporary dance.
c) It made her study other dancers carefully.
d) It kept her away from dancing for a whole year.
questions.explanation: During the injury she "started to watch other dancers more carefully" and "noticed small details in their movements." She could not dance "for four months", not a year, and she started contemporary dance at eleven, before the injury.

questions.question: Why did one of the judges like Isla’s audition?
options: a) She performed her piece without a single mistake.
b) She was able to dance in two different styles.
c) She carried on calmly after she slipped.
d) She chose a piece by a well-known dancer.
questions.explanation: Isla slipped but "just carried on and smiled", and the judge "liked that moment the most" because "it showed my character." So the performance was not perfect, and the piece was "by my own teacher", not a famous dancer.

questions.question: Read the text "From the sofa to the finish line". Which sentence (A–H) best fits gap 1?
questions.explanation: The text moves from his old life ("hardly ever did any exercise") to "His doctor told him"; a "check-up at his local surgery" is where this happened, and "Everything changed" marks the turning point. The sentence about running ten kilometres the next morning cannot fit, because Owen "could not run for a bus".
options: A) Carys agreed to run the whole race next to him.
B) Everything changed after a routine check-up at his local surgery.
C) For ten days he could not run at all, and he began to worry that he had lost all his fitness.
D) Luckily, the sunny weather made his long weekend runs a pleasure.
E) At first, even this was hard, and he often had to stop and rest.
F) Because of this, he still had energy for the last and most difficult part of the race.
G) The next morning, he ran ten kilometres without stopping.
H) He had never run further than five kilometres, and a marathon is more than forty-two.

questions.question: Read the text "From the sofa to the finish line". Which sentence (A–H) best fits gap 2?
questions.explanation: "even this" refers to the gentle mix of "one minute of running with ninety seconds of walking", and "At first" contrasts with "After nine weeks, however". The sentence about running ten kilometres the next morning is wrong, because after nine weeks he could only run "for thirty minutes", and he started with "something small".
options: A) Carys agreed to run the whole race next to him.
B) Everything changed after a routine check-up at his local surgery.
C) For ten days he could not run at all, and he began to worry that he had lost all his fitness.
D) Luckily, the sunny weather made his long weekend runs a pleasure.
E) At first, even this was hard, and he often had to stop and rest.
F) Because of this, he still had energy for the last and most difficult part of the race.
G) The next morning, he ran ten kilometres without stopping.
H) He had never run further than five kilometres, and a marathon is more than forty-two.

questions.question: Read the text "From the sofa to the finish line". Which sentence (A–H) best fits gap 3?
questions.explanation: This sentence explains why "Owen laughed at first": he had never run far, and a marathon is very long. "However" in the next sentence then introduces the answer to this problem, the "training plan for beginners". The sentence saying Carys agreed to run next to him is wrong, because at the end she "was waiting at the finish line".
options: A) Carys agreed to run the whole race next to him.
B) Everything changed after a routine check-up at his local surgery.
C) For ten days he could not run at all, and he began to worry that he had lost all his fitness.
D) Luckily, the sunny weather made his long weekend runs a pleasure.
E) At first, even this was hard, and he often had to stop and rest.
F) Because of this, he still had energy for the last and most difficult part of the race.
G) The next morning, he ran ten kilometres without stopping.
H) He had never run further than five kilometres, and a marathon is more than forty-two.

questions.question: Read the text "From the sofa to the finish line". Which sentence (A–H) best fits gap 4?
questions.explanation: After "caught a bad cold", this sentence describes the result: he "could not run at all" and was worried. This leads to "Instead of giving up". The sentence about sunny weather contradicts "the weather was terrible".
options: A) Carys agreed to run the whole race next to him.
B) Everything changed after a routine check-up at his local surgery.
C) For ten days he could not run at all, and he began to worry that he had lost all his fitness.
D) Luckily, the sunny weather made his long weekend runs a pleasure.
E) At first, even this was hard, and he often had to stop and rest.
F) Because of this, he still had energy for the last and most difficult part of the race.
G) The next morning, he ran ten kilometres without stopping.
H) He had never run further than five kilometres, and a marathon is more than forty-two.

questions.question: Read the text "From the sofa to the finish line". Which sentence (A–H) best fits gap 5?
questions.explanation: "Because of this" refers to "started slowly": by not running too fast at the beginning, he still had energy at the end, and then "He finished". The sentence saying Carys ran the race next to him is wrong, because she "was waiting at the finish line".
options: A) Carys agreed to run the whole race next to him.
B) Everything changed after a routine check-up at his local surgery.
C) For ten days he could not run at all, and he began to worry that he had lost all his fitness.
D) Luckily, the sunny weather made his long weekend runs a pleasure.
E) At first, even this was hard, and he often had to stop and rest.
F) Because of this, he still had energy for the last and most difficult part of the race.
G) The next morning, he ran ten kilometres without stopping.
H) He had never run further than five kilometres, and a marathon is more than forty-two.

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits gap (1).
questions.explanation: You apply for a job: "I saw a notice in the window and applied for it". Offered for, signed for (receive a parcel) and filled for do not mean asking to be given a job.
options: a) applied
b) offered
c) signed
d) filled

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits gap (2).
questions.explanation: The collocation is ask a question: "Mrs Hughes asked me a few questions about myself". We do not say made, did or said questions to someone.
options: a) did
b) asked
c) said
d) made

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits gap (3).
questions.explanation: The writer was told "I could start the following Saturday", meaning the next one. The last or previous Saturday is in the past, so the writer cannot start then, and the early Saturday has no meaning.
options: a) previous
b) early
c) last
d) following

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits gap (4).
questions.explanation: You wear clothes: "I had to wear a green shirt". Dress needs a person as object (dress a child), put needs on (put on a shirt) and try also needs on (try on a shirt).
options: a) put
b) try
c) wear
d) dress

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits gap (5).
questions.explanation: The writer spent the morning "learning how to use the till", the machine for taking money. Do and make the till are not possible, and hold the till does not mean operating it.
options: a) hold
b) use
c) do
d) make

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits gap (6).
questions.explanation: The collocation is make a mistake: "I made lots of mistakes", followed by two examples. Did, got and had mistakes are not correct English.
options: a) made
b) had
c) did
d) got

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (1).
questions.explanation: Whose is the possessive relative pronoun: "a girl whose name was Isla" means a girl, and her name was Isla. Who or that cannot be followed directly by a noun like name.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (2).
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is keen on something: "I was not very keen on the idea". No other preposition is used after keen with a noun.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (3).
questions.explanation: Even though introduces a surprising contrast: they chatted every weekend "even though we had never met". Only even fits before though in one word here.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (4).
questions.explanation: What means the thing that and starts the subject of the clause: "and what worried me most was that we would have nothing to say". No other single word can start this clause.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (5).
questions.explanation: There was introduces something that exists (or here, does not exist): "there was no reason to worry at all". It was no reason is not correct English.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (6).
questions.explanation: The fixed pattern is a + noun + of + my own: "had a little room of my own", meaning a room only for the writer. No other word fits after of my.

questions.question:
Read this email from your English-speaking friend Tom and the notes you have made.

From: Tom
Subject: Our cooking evening

Hi!
I’m really looking forward to the cooking evening we’re organising for our class next Friday. [Note 1: Me too!] About twelve people are coming. Should we cook one big meal together or ask everyone to bring a dish? [Note 2: Say which and why] I can bring plates and glasses from my house. What else do we need? [Note 3: Tell Tom] Also, my cousin Ellie is staying with us that weekend. Is it all right if she comes too? [Note 4: Yes, because …]

Cheers,
Tom

Write your email to Tom using all the notes. Write about 100 words.
questions.explanation:
A good answer replies to all four notes: (1) says you are also looking forward to the evening; (2) chooses between cooking one big meal and asking everyone to bring a dish, and gives a reason; (3) tells Tom what else you need, for example food, drinks or kitchen things; (4) agrees that Ellie can come and says why. Use an informal greeting and ending, link your ideas and write about 100 words.

Model answer:
Hi Tom,
Me too – I can’t wait! It’s going to be great fun.
I think we should cook one big meal together, like a pasta dish. That way everyone can help in the kitchen, and it’s cheaper than buying lots of different things.
Thanks for the plates and glasses. We’ll also need some big pans, a few sharp knives and something to drink. I can get the vegetables from the market on Thursday.
Of course Ellie can come! The more people we have, the better, and she can meet everyone in our class.
See you on Friday,
Maria

questions.question:
Choose ONE of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

Question 2 – Article
You see this announcement on an English-language website for teenagers.

Articles wanted!
MY FAVOURITE MEAL
What is your favourite meal? Who makes it, and when do you usually eat it? Why do you like it so much?
Write an article answering these questions. The best articles will appear on our website next month.

Write your article.

Question 3 – Story
Your English teacher has asked you to write a story.
Your story must begin with this sentence:
Suddenly there was smoke everywhere in the kitchen.

Write your story.
questions.explanation:
Article: give your article a title, answer every question in the announcement (the meal, who makes it and when, why you like it) and make it interesting for the reader, for example by describing the taste or a special memory. Story: begin with the given sentence, use past tenses, and give the story a clear development and ending. In both tasks write about 100 words.

Model article:
Granny’s Sunday soup
My favourite meal is a vegetable soup that my grandmother makes. We eat it every Sunday when the whole family visits her flat.
She puts in carrots, potatoes, beans and lots of herbs from her small garden, and she always serves it with warm bread that she bakes herself. It smells wonderful as soon as you open the door!
Why do I love it so much? Partly because it tastes delicious, but mostly because it reminds me of happy afternoons with my cousins, talking and laughing around her little kitchen table.

Model story:
Suddenly there was smoke everywhere in the kitchen. I had wanted to surprise my parents with a special breakfast, but I had forgotten about the toast while I was making the eggs.
I opened all the windows and threw the black bread into the bin. Just then the smoke alarm started ringing loudly, and my dad ran downstairs in his pyjamas.
“What’s happening?” he shouted. When he saw the plates on the table, he started to smile.
In the end we ate eggs without toast, and Dad said it was the best breakfast he had ever had.

questions.question:
Part 1 – Interview
The examiner asks you some questions about yourself. Answer each question and give some extra information.

Do you like spending time outdoors? Why or why not?
Where do you go when you want to be in nature?
What did you do the last time you went to the countryside or the beach?
Which season do you like best? Why?
Would you like to go camping? Why or why not?
questions.explanation:
Give full answers: answer the question, then add a reason or an example. Use the past simple for the question about the last time you went somewhere, and would for the question about camping.

Model answers:
Yes, I love it. After a day at school I need some fresh air, so I often go for a walk or ride my bike.
There’s a big forest about twenty minutes from my town. My family goes there at weekends to walk and have picnics.
Last summer I went to the beach with my cousins. We swam in the sea and played volleyball on the sand all afternoon.
I like autumn best, because the trees turn red and orange and it isn’t too hot to go hiking.
I’d love to try it, but only in summer! I think it would be exciting to sleep under the stars.

questions.question:
Part 2 – Photo description
Look at the photograph. It shows four young people collecting rubbish on a sandy beach. They are all wearing gloves, and two of them are holding large black bags. One of them is picking up a plastic bottle from the sand. Next to them there are some more bags full of rubbish. Behind them you can see the sea and some rocks, and the sky is blue. Tell us what you can see in the photograph.

Talk for about one minute.
questions.explanation:
Describe the place, the people and what they are doing, using the present continuous (are collecting, is picking up). Say where things are (next to them, behind them). If you do not know a word, explain it in other words. Only describe what is in the photo; you can say what you think about it, but do not invent new details.

Model answer:
This photo was taken on a sandy beach. I can see four young people, and they’re collecting rubbish. They’re all wearing gloves to protect their hands. Two of them are holding large black bags, and one of them is picking up a plastic bottle from the sand. Next to them there are some more bags, and they’re full of rubbish, so I think they’ve been working for a while. Behind them I can see the sea and some rocks, and the sky is blue, so the weather looks nice. I think what they’re doing is really useful for the beach.

questions.question:
Part 3 – Collaborative task
A school wants to do more to help the environment. Here are some ideas the students are thinking about.

recycling bins in every classroom
a vegetable garden in the school grounds
a week when everyone walks or cycles to school
turning off lights and computers at lunchtime
a sale of second-hand uniforms and books
solar panels on the school roof

Talk together about how each idea could help the environment. Then decide which idea the school should try first.

Talk together for about two or three minutes.
questions.explanation:
Discuss the ideas one by one and give reasons for your opinions. Ask your partner what they think, agree and disagree politely, and try to make a decision together at the end. Useful language: How about …? I’m not sure that … would work. That’s a good idea because … Let’s go for …

Model conversation (part):
A: Let’s start with the recycling bins. They’re cheap and easy to put in every classroom.
B: That’s true, but many schools already have them. What do you think about the solar panels?
A: They’d save a lot of energy, but they’re very expensive. I don’t think the school can pay for them.
B: Good point. The vegetable garden is nice too, because students learn where food comes from.
A: Yes, but it needs a lot of work, and who looks after it in the holidays?
B: Hmm. So maybe the walking and cycling week? Everyone can join in, and it costs nothing.
A: I agree. Let’s choose that one first.

questions.question:
Part 4 – General conversation
The examiner asks you and your partner some questions about recycling and protecting nature. Give your opinion and talk to your partner too.

What do you and your family recycle at home?
Do you think people throw away too many things? Why?
What can young people do to protect nature?
Is it better to buy new things or second-hand things? Why?
Have you ever taken part in an activity to help the environment?
questions.explanation:
Give your opinion with a reason or an example, and respond to your partner (I see what you mean, but …; Me too!). Use the present perfect with ever for the last question.

Model answers:
We recycle paper, glass and plastic. We have three different bins in the kitchen, and my brother takes them out every Thursday.
Yes, definitely. People often buy new phones or clothes when the old ones still work perfectly well.
They can use less plastic, walk or cycle instead of asking for a lift, and tell their friends why it’s important.
It depends. For clothes and books, second-hand is great because it’s cheaper and better for the planet. But I’d buy some things new, like shoes.
Yes, once. Our class planted trees in a park near our school. It was hard work, but I felt really proud.

questions.question: What is wrong with the woman’s phone?
options: a) The screen is broken.
b) The battery is weak.
c) The camera doesn’t work.
questions.explanation: The woman says "the camera doesn’t work any more". She also says "the screen didn’t break" and "the battery’s fine too".

questions.question: How much will the woman pay for the repair?
questions.explanation: The man says "it’s just forty-five" because there is "fifteen pounds off all keyboards this month". £75 is the normal price, and the woman wrongly thinks it will be £60 until he says "Less than that, actually".

questions.question: Where did the man find his tablet?
options: a) On the bus
b) In a café
c) In the library
questions.explanation: He had used it "in the café after I left the library", and "The waiter had kept it behind the counter". The bus company "didn’t have it".

questions.question: Which computer is the woman going to buy?
options: a) A small laptop
b) A desktop computer
c) A tablet with a keyboard
questions.explanation: The woman says "I’m going for the desktop computer". The laptop screen is "too small for my design work", and she does not need the tablet because "I always work at home".

questions.question: What time will the engineer arrive tomorrow?
options: a) At two o’clock
b) At nine o’clock
c) At half past eleven
questions.explanation: The message says "she’ll be with you at two o’clock". Nine o’clock was the time of the first booking, and the new engineer is "busy until half past eleven".

questions.question: What does the man buy?
options: a) A phone case
b) Some earphones
c) A phone charger
questions.explanation: The man says "I’ll just take the charger, then". The phone cases are only where the chargers are, and the earphones have "sold out".

questions.question: What did the woman learn on her computer course?
options: a) How to improve photos
b) How to make games
c) How to build a website
questions.explanation: She "did the one on photos instead" and can now "make all my holiday pictures look professional". The website course "was full", and she does not want to make games with her son.

questions.question: You will hear two friends talking about a new food waste bin. What does the woman think of it?
options: a) It is not worth the trouble.
b) It makes the kitchen smell bad.
c) It has made things easier.
questions.explanation: The woman says "it’s made life easier" because they only take the rubbish out "once a week". She expected a smell, but says "Not at all". It is the man who is "not sure it’s worth all the trouble".

questions.question: You will hear two friends talking about second-hand clothes. Why does the woman buy them?
options: a) To save money
b) Because she prefers older styles
c) To help reduce waste
questions.explanation: After a programme about how many clothes "get thrown away every year", she decided to "try not to buy anything new". About money she says "Some of those shops aren’t cheap" and "that isn’t why I do it", and about the seventies look she says "Not especially".

questions.question: You will hear two parents talking about a new rule at their children’s school. What do they agree about?
options: a) The children will soon lose their bottles.
b) The school should provide the bottles.
c) The new rule is unlikely to work.
questions.explanation: The woman says "the school should give them one each" and the man answers "You’re right". She thinks the rule is "a good idea", and when she says her son will lose his bottle, the man replies "I don’t think so".

questions.question: You will hear a man telling a friend about cycling to work. How does he feel about it?
options: a) Surprised that he enjoys it so much
b) Worried about the traffic on the main road
c) Annoyed that the journey takes longer
questions.explanation: He says "I actually look forward to it now. I never thought I’d say that!" He feels "quite safe" because of the cycle path, and it is "only five minutes slower" than driving.

questions.question: You will hear a woman telling a friend about a beach clean-up. What does she say about it?
options: a) It was badly organised.
b) It made her change how she shops.
c) Not enough people took part.
questions.explanation: She was shocked by the "plastic packaging", and "Since then I’ve been taking my own containers to the market". She says it was "Really well organised", and "about forty of us" came.

questions.question: You will hear two friends talking about a journey. Why did the man decide to go by train?
options: a) To cause less pollution
b) Because it was cheaper than flying
c) Because he is afraid of flying
questions.explanation: He read "how much pollution one flight makes" and wanted to travel in a way that is "better for the planet". The train "cost more than the plane", and he is not scared because he flies "for work all the time".

questions.question: Meeting point: the car park next to the ____
questions.explanation: "We’ll all meet in the car park next to the old mill". The bridge in the town centre was last year’s meeting place.

questions.question: Start time: ____
questions.explanation: The poster says ten o’clock, but "that was a mistake": "We’ll actually start at half past nine".

questions.question: Volunteers must bring their own ____.
questions.explanation: Bags and litter pickers are given out, "so you won’t need to bring those. What you do need to bring is a pair of gloves."

questions.question: Strangest thing found in the river last year: a ____
questions.explanation: Bottles, cans and shopping trolleys are found every year, "But the strangest thing we pulled out last year was a guitar."

questions.question: Free lunch will be brought by a local ____.
questions.explanation: "The café by the river has closed down … but a local bakery has kindly offered to bring sandwiches and cakes".

questions.question: Children under ____ must come with an adult.
questions.explanation: "Anyone under fourteen must be with an adult." Twelve was the age "last year".

questions.question: Why did Leo first go climbing?
options: a) He hoped to find a sport he was good at.
b) He was invited to a friend’s birthday party.
c) He was bored, so he went with his sister.
questions.explanation: "The next week I went along with her, just because I was bored." It was his sister who went to the birthday party, and he "didn’t expect much", so he was not looking for a sport.

questions.question: What does Leo enjoy most about climbing?
options: a) Meeting other young climbers at competitions
b) Working out how to climb a route
c) Becoming stronger and fitter
questions.explanation: "For me the best part is the puzzle … you have to work out where to put your hands and feet." He says you need strength, but "people think" it is all about that.

questions.question: How does Leo feel about climbing outdoors?
options: a) He prefers it to indoor walls.
b) It is too far away to do often.
c) It is more useful for training.
questions.explanation: "Nothing compares to being on real rock in the mountains." Climbing walls are the ones that are "great for practising", so outdoor climbing is not better for training.

questions.question: What is Leo’s opinion about the danger of climbing?
options: a) It is safer than many people believe.
b) His mother is right to worry about him.
c) Most accidents happen to beginners.
questions.explanation: "It’s much safer than most people imagine." He says accidents happen "when people get careless", not that they happen to beginners.

questions.question: What does Leo say about his teachers?
options: a) They let him miss homework before competitions.
b) They help him keep up with his schoolwork.
c) They think he should train less often.
questions.explanation: His teachers "sent me work to do so that I didn’t fall behind". He still does his homework "on the bus and at lunchtime", and they are "really understanding" about his training.

questions.question: How does Leo feel about his future?
options: a) He is afraid he will get bored with the sport.
b) He is determined to compete in the Olympics.
c) He wants to concentrate on enjoying climbing.
questions.explanation: "Right now I just want to keep enjoying it." The Olympics "would be incredible", but "I try not to think that far ahead".

questions.question: What does the sign say?
options: a) Owners can ask to wait somewhere calmer.
b) Cats and dogs must wait in separate rooms.
c) Nervous animals will be seen by the vet first.
questions.explanation: If a pet is nervous, owners should "tell reception and we will find you a quieter place to wait". The sign says nothing about seeing nervous animals first, and cats and dogs share the waiting room, as long as dogs are "on a short lead" and cats are "in a closed basket".

questions.question: What does the notice say?
options: a) Staff will test your aquarium water free of charge.
b) Two large tubs come with a free gift.
c) The offer will continue after Saturday.
questions.explanation: If you "Buy two large tubs" you "get a free water-testing kit". The offer "ends Saturday" or earlier, and staff help you "choose the right food" – they do not test the water for you.

questions.question: What does the message tell Mrs Doyle?
options: a) She can collect Biscuit at any time today.
b) She needs to call the vet before she comes.
c) Biscuit can have a little food this evening.
questions.explanation: The message says Biscuit "mustn’t eat anything until this evening, and only a little then", so a small amount of food is fine this evening. She can only be collected "after 3", not at any time, and Mrs Doyle only needs to call "if you have any questions".

questions.question: Who can join the classes?
options: a) Puppies that are under ten weeks old
b) Young puppies that have had all their injections
c) Any dog whose owner books a place at the till
questions.explanation: Puppies "must be between 10 and 20 weeks old and must have had all their injections". Booking at the till is necessary but not enough – older dogs cannot join – and puppies under ten weeks are too young.

questions.question: What is changing at the surgery?
options: a) Clients will need a new number for all emergencies.
b) It will be moving to new premises in Hillbrook.
c) It will close one afternoon each week.
questions.explanation: The surgery "will be closed on Wednesday afternoons" from next month. The clinic number is only for emergencies "at these times", not for all emergencies, and Hillbrook is where the "partner clinic" is – the surgery itself is not moving.

questions.question: Jamie, who is 17, loves animals and wants a job outdoors. He lives in London, a long way from most of the jobs advertised, so he will need somewhere to stay.
options: A) Tourist Information Centre, Edinburgh
B) Pets Corner, Bristol
C) Sunshine Sports Camp, Cardiff
D) Open-top Bus Guide, York
E) Hilltop Farm Park, Cumbria
F) Little Artists Holiday Club, Norwich
G) Seaview Hotel Kitchen, Cornwall
H) The Corner Café, Brighton
questions.explanation: At Hilltop Farm Park you "feed the goats, sheep and rabbits", you will be "outside in all weathers", and staff who live far away "can stay free of charge in the farm’s cottage". Pets Corner also involves animals, but "Most of the work is indoors" and "we cannot help with accommodation".

questions.question: Zara speaks fluent Spanish and wants a job where she can use it with visitors to Britain. She has classes every afternoon, so she can only work in the mornings.
options: A) Tourist Information Centre, Edinburgh
B) Pets Corner, Bristol
C) Sunshine Sports Camp, Cardiff
D) Open-top Bus Guide, York
E) Hilltop Farm Park, Cumbria
F) Little Artists Holiday Club, Norwich
G) Seaview Hotel Kitchen, Cornwall
H) The Corner Café, Brighton
questions.explanation: The Tourist Information Centre helps visitors, "Speakers of a second language such as French, Spanish or Italian are especially welcome", and "Shifts run from 8 am to 1 pm". The bus guide job also pays more for another language, but tours run "from 2 pm" until 8 pm, when Zara has classes.

questions.question: Ben wants to earn as much money as possible this summer because he is saving for a car. He enjoys cooking and is happy to work full-time.
options: A) Tourist Information Centre, Edinburgh
B) Pets Corner, Bristol
C) Sunshine Sports Camp, Cardiff
D) Open-top Bus Guide, York
E) Hilltop Farm Park, Cumbria
F) Little Artists Holiday Club, Norwich
G) Seaview Hotel Kitchen, Cornwall
H) The Corner Café, Brighton
questions.explanation: At the Seaview Hotel you "prepare breakfasts and help our chefs", the pay is "well above the usual rate", and it is "full-time work only". The Corner Café also involves cooking, but "The pay is the minimum rate" and help is needed "only at weekends".

questions.question: Chloe is a strong swimmer and has a lifeguard certificate. She is hoping to find a job where she can use it, and she’d like to work with children.
options: A) Tourist Information Centre, Edinburgh
B) Pets Corner, Bristol
C) Sunshine Sports Camp, Cardiff
D) Open-top Bus Guide, York
E) Hilltop Farm Park, Cumbria
F) Little Artists Holiday Club, Norwich
G) Seaview Hotel Kitchen, Cornwall
H) The Corner Café, Brighton
questions.explanation: The Sunshine Sports Camp runs "swimming sessions for children aged seven to twelve", and "You must hold a lifeguard certificate to work in the pool". The Little Artists Holiday Club also works with children, but only with "painting, model-making and other craft activities", so Chloe could not use her certificate.

questions.question: Ellie is studying art and would like a summer job with young children. She needs to finish work by three o’clock every day because she looks after her little brother in the afternoons.
options: A) Tourist Information Centre, Edinburgh
B) Pets Corner, Bristol
C) Sunshine Sports Camp, Cardiff
D) Open-top Bus Guide, York
E) Hilltop Farm Park, Cumbria
F) Little Artists Holiday Club, Norwich
G) Seaview Hotel Kitchen, Cornwall
H) The Corner Café, Brighton
questions.explanation: The Little Artists Holiday Club needs help with "children aged four to seven" doing painting and crafts, and it "runs from 9 am to 2.30 pm". The Sunshine Sports Camp is also for children, but the hours are "9 am to 5 pm" and the activities are sports, not art.

questions.question: Why did Priya make her first video?
options: a) Her teacher asked her to make one for the class.
b) She wanted to help a relative with a subject.
c) She hoped to become well known online.
d) She needed it for a school chemistry project.
questions.explanation: Her cousin "was having the same problem with chemistry, so she filmed the next experiment for him." Her teacher only started using the videos later, and the text says she "never planned to become a video maker".

questions.question: Why does Priya spend so much time on research?
options: a) Her viewers often point out her mistakes.
b) Her brother taught her to check facts carefully.
c) Her teacher checks each video before she posts it.
d) She thinks wrong information is worse than none.
questions.explanation: Priya says: "A mistake in a science video is worse than no video at all." Her brother helped her with a microphone and editing, not with checking facts, and the unkind comments were about the poor sound and her fast talking.

questions.question: What does Mr Evans suggest about Priya’s videos?
options: a) They use some language that he does not like.
b) Students should watch them at home, not in class.
c) Students pay more attention to her than to him.
d) They are too simple for his older students.
questions.explanation: Mr Evans says students "listen to her in a different way. They listen to me because they have to!" He likes the way she uses "the language of teenagers", and he shows the videos "in his lessons".

questions.question: Why has Priya refused the offers from companies?
options: a) She does not want to lose her viewers’ trust.
b) Her parents do not allow her to advertise.
c) She has no time to make extra videos for them.
d) The money they offered was too little.
questions.explanation: Priya says: "My viewers trust me. I don’t want them to think I’m selling something." The text says nothing about the amount of money, her parents or a lack of time.

questions.question: Which of these would Priya probably write on her channel page?
options: a) Kitchen Lab: I make these videos with my teacher, and we post a new one every day.
b) Kitchen Lab: easy science with things from your kitchen. Young viewers, ask an adult first!
c) Kitchen Lab: science videos for future doctors, with special offers from our sponsors.
d) Kitchen Lab: real experiments with the chemicals that scientists use in their laboratories.
questions.explanation: "Every experiment uses things from an ordinary kitchen" and she "reminds younger viewers to ask an adult for help." She "never uses dangerous chemicals", she films on Sunday afternoons (not every day) without her teacher, and she has said no to every company.

questions.question: Read the text "Six pupils and one teacher". Which sentence (A–H) best fits gap 1?
questions.explanation: "Their" refers to the six pupils, and "Their only teacher" introduces the person who is named next: "Fiona MacLeod has worked at the school for nine years". The sentence saying the children have dozens of friends of their own age is impossible on an island where the school has "just six pupils".
options: A) Then she moves around the room and spends time with each of them in turn.
B) If the numbers keep falling, the local council may decide to close the school.
C) As a result, they have dozens of friends of their own age on the island.
D) Because of this, school trips to museums or theatres are very rare.
E) On Saturdays, the children love going shopping at the busy market in the harbour.
F) Their only teacher is also the head teacher, the cook and sometimes the gardener.
G) For this reason, the youngest pupils are never allowed to work with the older ones.
H) Fiona understands this worry, but she has found ways to solve the problem.

questions.question: Read the text "Six pupils and one teacher". Which sentence (A–H) best fits gap 2?
questions.explanation: "Then" follows "Every morning, Fiona gives each pupil a plan", and "each of them" refers to the pupils. The sentence saying the youngest pupils never work with the older ones is wrong, because the next sentence says "The older ones often help the younger ones".
options: A) Then she moves around the room and spends time with each of them in turn.
B) If the numbers keep falling, the local council may decide to close the school.
C) As a result, they have dozens of friends of their own age on the island.
D) Because of this, school trips to museums or theatres are very rare.
E) On Saturdays, the children love going shopping at the busy market in the harbour.
F) Their only teacher is also the head teacher, the cook and sometimes the gardener.
G) For this reason, the youngest pupils are never allowed to work with the older ones.
H) Fiona understands this worry, but she has found ways to solve the problem.

questions.question: Read the text "Six pupils and one teacher". Which sentence (A–H) best fits gap 3?
questions.explanation: "Because of this" refers to the island having "no shops" and a ferry that "only sails three times a week", so trips are rare. "Instead, the children use the island itself as a classroom" then follows naturally. The sentence about shopping at a busy market contradicts "no shops apart from a small post office".
options: A) Then she moves around the room and spends time with each of them in turn.
B) If the numbers keep falling, the local council may decide to close the school.
C) As a result, they have dozens of friends of their own age on the island.
D) Because of this, school trips to museums or theatres are very rare.
E) On Saturdays, the children love going shopping at the busy market in the harbour.
F) Their only teacher is also the head teacher, the cook and sometimes the gardener.
G) For this reason, the youngest pupils are never allowed to work with the older ones.
H) Fiona understands this worry, but she has found ways to solve the problem.

questions.question: Read the text "Six pupils and one teacher". Which sentence (A–H) best fits gap 4?
questions.explanation: "this worry" refers to "Some people worry that the children do not have enough friends", and the "ways to solve the problem" are the visits to the mainland school and the video calls. The sentence saying they have dozens of friends on the island cannot follow a worry about too few friends.
options: A) Then she moves around the room and spends time with each of them in turn.
B) If the numbers keep falling, the local council may decide to close the school.
C) As a result, they have dozens of friends of their own age on the island.
D) Because of this, school trips to museums or theatres are very rare.
E) On Saturdays, the children love going shopping at the busy market in the harbour.
F) Their only teacher is also the head teacher, the cook and sometimes the gardener.
G) For this reason, the youngest pupils are never allowed to work with the older ones.
H) Fiona understands this worry, but she has found ways to solve the problem.

questions.question: Read the text "Six pupils and one teacher". Which sentence (A–H) best fits gap 5?
questions.explanation: Two pupils will leave and "only one new child is expected", so the numbers are falling, and this sentence explains the danger. "But Fiona is hopeful" then contrasts with it. It also explains "The biggest problem for the school is its future". The sentence about dozens of friends on the island cannot fit here, because the school is getting smaller.
options: A) Then she moves around the room and spends time with each of them in turn.
B) If the numbers keep falling, the local council may decide to close the school.
C) As a result, they have dozens of friends of their own age on the island.
D) Because of this, school trips to museums or theatres are very rare.
E) On Saturdays, the children love going shopping at the busy market in the harbour.
F) Their only teacher is also the head teacher, the cook and sometimes the gardener.
G) For this reason, the youngest pupils are never allowed to work with the older ones.
H) Fiona understands this worry, but she has found ways to solve the problem.

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits gap (1).
questions.explanation: Only invite follows the pattern verb + person + to-infinitive: "he invited me to spend a weekend bird watching with him". We cannot say offered me to, suggested me to or agreed me to.
options: a) invited
b) suggested
c) agreed
d) offered

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits gap (2).
questions.explanation: The collocation is make a noise: they "tried not to make any noise, because even a cough can frighten birds away". Do, give and take a noise are not correct English.
options: a) give
b) take
c) make
d) do

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits gap (3).
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is catch sight of, meaning see something suddenly: "I suddenly caught sight of a flash of bright blue". Took sight, held sight and got sight are not used.
options: a) took
b) held
c) got
d) caught

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits gap (4).
questions.explanation: Manage is followed by a to-infinitive: "I was amazed when I managed to take a photo of it". Succeeded needs in + -ing, could has no to, and achieved needs a noun object.
options: a) could
b) achieved
c) managed
d) succeeded

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits gap (5).
questions.explanation: To keep a notebook or diary means to write in it regularly: "He keeps a notebook in which he writes down every bird he sees". Saves, stores and collects a notebook do not describe writing a record in it.
options: a) stores
b) keeps
c) collects
d) saves

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits gap (6).
questions.explanation: Take up means start a new hobby: "I never expected to enjoy it so much, but now I have taken up bird watching myself". Given up would mean the writer stopped, which does not fit "enjoy it so much"; made up and put up have no connection with hobbies.
options: a) given
b) made
c) put
d) taken

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (1).
questions.explanation: In a negative sentence we use any with plural nouns: "we did not have any eggs at all". The words at all show that the answer is any, not some or many.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (2).
questions.explanation: So + adverb + that shows a result: the sauce boiled "for so long that it turned into a thick brown paste". Too or very cannot be followed by a that-clause of result.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (3).
questions.explanation: The pattern is too + adjective + for someone + to-infinitive: the rice became "too salty for anyone to eat". So or very cannot be followed by for anyone to eat.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (4).
questions.explanation: Apart from means except: "nothing on the table at all, apart from a plate of burnt bread". Apart is always followed by from in this meaning.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (5).
questions.explanation: Where introduces a relative clause about a place: "the little Italian restaurant where my parents had their first date". Which or that would need at at the end of the clause.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (6).
questions.explanation: The pattern for time needed is it + take + time + to-infinitive: "it took us nearly two hours to clean the kitchen". The subject must be the empty pronoun it.

questions.question:
Read this email from your English-speaking friend Priya and the notes you have made.

From: Priya
Subject: Getting fit together

Hi!
I’ve decided I really need to get fitter this year, and I’d love to do it with you. [Note 1: Great idea!] We could go running in the park or join the new sports centre in town. Which would you rather do? [Note 2: Choose and explain] How often do you think we should exercise? [Note 3: Suggest] I’d also like to eat more healthily, but I don’t know where to start. Have you got any tips? [Note 4: Give advice]

Speak soon,
Priya

Write your email to Priya using all the notes. Write about 100 words.
questions.explanation:
A good answer replies to all four notes: (1) says it is a great idea to get fit together; (2) chooses between running in the park and joining the sports centre, with a reason; (3) suggests how often you should exercise; (4) gives Priya at least one piece of advice about healthy eating. Use an informal greeting and ending, link your ideas and write about 100 words.

Model answer:
Hi Priya,
What a great idea! I’ve been feeling lazy recently, so I’d love to get fit with you.
I’d rather go running in the park. It’s free, we can go whenever we want, and it’s nice to be outside. The sports centre is quite expensive.
I think we should start with three times a week, maybe for half an hour, and then run a bit further each week.
About food, my advice is to eat fruit instead of crisps between meals and to drink lots of water. It really helps!
Let’s start on Monday.
Daniel

questions.question:
Choose ONE of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

Question 2 – Article
You see this announcement in your school’s English-language magazine.

Articles wanted!
HOW I KEEP HEALTHY
What do you do to keep healthy? What do you eat, and what kind of exercise do you do? Is there anything you would like to change?
Write an article answering these questions. We will publish the most interesting articles.

Write your article.

Question 3 – Story
Your English teacher has asked you to write a story.
Your story must begin with this sentence:
I had never run so fast in my life.

Write your story.
questions.explanation:
Article: give your article a title, answer all the questions in the announcement (food, exercise, something you would like to change) and talk directly to the reader to make it interesting. Story: begin with the given sentence, explain why you were running, and give the story a clear ending. Use past tenses consistently. In both tasks write about 100 words.

Model article:
Small habits, big difference
I’m not a sports star, but I try to keep healthy in simple ways. I cycle to school every day, even when it’s raining, and I play basketball with my friends on Saturdays.
I eat a big breakfast, usually porridge with fruit, and my family cooks fresh food most evenings. I don’t drink fizzy drinks any more.
What would I like to change? I go to bed too late because I watch videos on my phone. I know sleep is important, so that’s my next challenge. What’s yours?

Model story:
I had never run so fast in my life. The last train home was leaving at ten o’clock, and I was still three streets away from the station.
I raced past the shops and down the stairs to the platform. The doors were starting to close, but a kind man saw me and held them open with his arm.
I jumped in and fell into a seat, completely out of breath. “Thank you so much!” I said.
He smiled. “No problem. I’m the driver, actually. I was just on my way to the front.”

questions.question:
Part 1 – Interview
The examiner asks you some questions about yourself. Answer each question and give some extra information.

What kind of music do you like listening to?
Do you prefer watching films at home or at the cinema? Why?
Tell us about a film you saw recently.
Do you enjoy reading? What kind of books do you like?
Can you play a musical instrument, or would you like to learn one?
questions.explanation:
Give full answers: answer the question, then add a reason or an example. Use the past simple when you talk about a film you saw, and would like for things you want to do in the future.

Model answers:
I mostly listen to pop and a bit of rock. I usually put my headphones on when I’m on the bus to school.
I prefer the cinema, because the screen is huge and the sound is amazing. But it’s expensive, so I watch most films at home.
Last weekend I saw an animated film about a robot who gets lost in space. It was funny, but quite sad at the end too.
Yes, I do. I like adventure stories and books about real people, especially sports stars.
I can’t play anything at the moment, but I’d really like to learn the guitar. My uncle plays, and he says he’ll teach me.

questions.question:
Part 2 – Photo description
Look at the photograph. It shows a street performer in a town square. The performer is standing on a small wooden box and juggling three balls. A crowd of people is standing in a circle around the box, watching. Some of them are clapping, and a child is sitting on an adult’s shoulders to see better. On the ground in front of the box there is an open hat with some coins in it. Behind the crowd there are some cafés with tables outside. Tell us what you can see in the photograph.

Talk for about one minute.
questions.explanation:
Describe the place, the people and what they are doing, using the present continuous (is juggling, are clapping). Say where things are (in front of, behind, around). If you do not know a word, explain it in other words, for example a person who throws and catches balls. Only describe what is in the photo; do not invent new details.

Model answer:
This photo shows a town square, and there’s a street performer there. The performer is standing on a small wooden box and juggling three balls – that means throwing them in the air and catching them. There’s a crowd of people standing in a circle around the box, and they’re all watching. Some of them are clapping, so I think they’re enjoying the show. I can also see a child who is sitting on an adult’s shoulders to see better. In front of the box there’s an open hat with some coins in it, so I think people give the performer some money. Behind the crowd there are some cafés with tables outside.

questions.question:
Part 3 – Collaborative task
A class is going on a day trip to a big city, and the students can choose one activity. Here are some activities they are thinking about.

a visit to a science museum
a musical at a theatre
a boat trip on the river
an art gallery with famous paintings
a walking tour of the old town
a tour of a football stadium

Talk together about why each activity might be interesting for the class. Then decide which activity the class should choose.

Talk together for about two or three minutes.
questions.explanation:
Discuss the activities one by one and give reasons. Ask for your partner’s opinion, agree and disagree politely, and make a decision together at the end. Useful language: What about …? I think … would be more fun than … Do you agree? Shall we go for …?

Model conversation (part):
A: What do you think about the science museum? There are usually lots of things you can try yourself.
B: Yes, that’s fun, but we often go to museums with school. The boat trip sounds different.
A: True, and you can see the most famous buildings from the river. But what if it rains?
B: Good point. The musical would be fine in any weather, and everyone likes music.
A: Maybe, but tickets are really expensive, and it’s in the evening, isn’t it?
B: Hmm, you’re right. Then I think the boat trip is the best choice. Most boats have a roof anyway.
A: OK, let’s choose the boat trip.

questions.question:
Part 4 – General conversation
The examiner asks you and your partner some questions about going out and entertainment. Give your opinion and talk to your partner too.

What do you like doing when you go out with your friends?
Have you ever been to a concert or a festival? What was it like?
Do you think going out is too expensive for young people? Why?
Is it better to go out in a big group or with one or two friends?
What new kind of entertainment would you like to try?
questions.explanation:
Give your opinion with a reason or an example, and react to your partner (That’s a good point; I’m not sure I agree, because …). Use the present perfect with ever, and the past simple to say what it was like.

Model answers:
Usually we go bowling or just walk around the centre and get something to eat.
Yes, I went to an open-air festival last summer. It was crowded and very loud, but the atmosphere was fantastic.
Sometimes, yes. Cinema tickets and concerts cost a lot, so we often stay at someone’s house and watch films instead.
I prefer a small group, because you can talk properly. In a big group it’s hard to decide what to do.
I’d like to try an escape room. My friends say it’s really exciting to solve the puzzles before the time runs out.

questions.question: What does the woman ask Tom to do first?
options: a) answer the emails
b) tidy the storeroom
c) phone a customer
questions.explanation: The woman says "the storeroom’s in a terrible mess. Could you sort that out first?" She asks him to leave the emails "until later today", and she will phone Mrs Green "myself".

questions.question: Where will the team meeting be?
options: a) in the café downstairs
b) in the staff kitchen
c) in Meeting Room Two
questions.explanation: The woman says "Let’s use the staff kitchen" and the man agrees. Meeting Room Two has "a problem with the heating", and the café is "too noisy".

questions.question: Where does the woman work now?
options: a) in a school
b) in a hotel
c) in a hospital
questions.explanation: The woman says "I’m working on reception at the Park Hotel". She has "left the hospital", and she did not become a teacher because "you need another year of training".

questions.question: What time will Dan start work next week?
options: a) at eight o’clock
b) at two o’clock
c) at six o’clock
questions.explanation: Dan is on the early shift and says "The early shift starts at six now". The woman wrongly guesses eight o’clock, and two o’clock is the afternoon shift he has been doing.

questions.question: What has the engineer come to repair?
options: a) the photocopier
b) the coffee machine
c) the printer
questions.explanation: The man says "I’m here for the photocopier". He says "I don’t do printers", and the woman only jokes about the coffee machine.

questions.question: What must the woman bring on her first day?
options: a) her bank details
b) her passport
c) a photo of herself
questions.explanation: The man says "we haven’t got your bank details yet, so please bring those". They saw her passport "at the interview", and they will take her photo themselves.

questions.question: Which part of her job does the woman enjoy most?
options: a) cutting the grass
b) talking to visitors
c) planting trees
questions.explanation: She says "the best part is in autumn, when we plant new trees". Cutting the grass "gets a bit boring", and talking to visitors is only "nice".

questions.question: You will hear a woman telling a friend about the cat she got from a rescue centre. Why did she choose an older cat?
options: a) It cost less than a kitten.
b) There were no kittens left.
c) She wanted a quiet animal.
questions.explanation: Kittens are "full of energy", but she says "I need peace and quiet", and her cat "just sleeps" by her desk. It was "the same price", and the centre "had lots of" kittens.

questions.question: You will hear two friends talking about dog training classes. What does the man think of them?
options: a) They cost more than they are worth.
b) He is learning a lot from them too.
c) His dog is too old to learn much.
questions.explanation: He says the trainer "teaches the owners" and "Most of the problems were my fault". The classes are "worth it", and Rocky is "only one, so he learns fast".

questions.question: You will hear two friends talking about a day at a wildlife park. What do they agree about?
options: a) The café was much too slow.
b) The animals were well cared for.
c) The entry tickets were too expensive.
questions.explanation: The man says the animals "looked healthy" and the woman answers "True. The keepers obviously care about them". She complains about the café, but he says "I didn’t mind that"; he thinks the price is "too much", but she thinks "it’s fair".

questions.question: You will hear a man talking about helping at a dog shelter. Why does he do it?
options: a) He cannot keep a dog at home.
b) He wants to get fitter.
c) He hopes to work with animals.
questions.explanation: He says "pets aren’t allowed in my flat", so at the shelter he can "spend time with dogs without breaking the rules". He already runs every day, "so that’s not the point", and he is "happy in my job".

questions.question: You will hear a woman talking to a friend about her daughter’s rabbit. How does she feel about it now?
options: a) Happy that it has become her pet too
b) Annoyed that she has to clean the cage
c) Worried that her daughter has lost interest
questions.explanation: She says "he’s really become my rabbit too" and "I’m quite glad she wanted one". She cleans the cage, but "I don’t mind at all", and she does not seem worried about her daughter.

questions.question: You will hear two friends talking about a TV programme. What is the man’s opinion of it?
options: a) It lasted much longer than necessary.
b) It was too sad to enjoy.
c) It changed his view of foxes.
questions.explanation: He "used to think foxes were just a nuisance", but says "I feel differently now". The sad part ended well ("it found its mother"), and it is the woman who thinks it was long; he "didn’t notice the time at all".

questions.question: The centre will be officially opened by a famous ____.
questions.explanation: "The centre will be officially opened by a well-known footballer". The story about a singer "isn’t true".

questions.question: Number of shops open on Saturday: ____
questions.explanation: "On Saturday there will be sixty-five shops open". Seventy was the number they "had hoped to have", but some are not ready.

questions.question: On the top floor: a food court and a ____
questions.explanation: "On the top floor there’s a cinema with six screens". The bowling alley "won’t be finished until next summer".

questions.question: Parking is free for the first ____.
questions.explanation: "Parking is free for the first two hours. After that it costs one pound an hour."

questions.question: Bus number ____ stops outside the main entrance.
questions.explanation: "The number forty-two bus stops right outside the main entrance." The number twenty-four "stops on the other side of the river".

questions.question: Free gift for each of the first 100 customers: an ____
questions.explanation: "The first hundred customers through the door will each get a free umbrella". Shopping bags are what "lots of new shopping centres" give away.

questions.question: How did Jess feel when she saw the note asking for a drummer?
options: a) Excited to join a band at last
b) Unsure if she could play well enough
c) Worried that she was too busy at college
questions.explanation: "I almost didn’t reply, because I didn’t think I was good enough." Her best friend had to make her go, so she was not excited.

questions.question: What does Jess say about recording the album?
options: a) She enjoyed it more than live concerts.
b) It taught her to be more patient.
c) It was easier than playing on stage.
questions.explanation: "It taught me a lot about being patient." It was "harder than I expected" and "some days I got really fed up", so it was not easier or more enjoyable.

questions.question: What does Jess think about the arguments in the band?
options: a) They make the music more interesting.
b) They make it hard to finish new songs.
c) They usually end with Sam getting his way.
questions.explanation: "I think that’s why our music works. If we all wanted the same thing, it would be boring." She never says the arguments stop them finishing songs.

questions.question: How does Jess feel about social media?
options: a) It has not helped the band to find fans.
b) She loves making videos to put online.
c) It is useful, but she dislikes it.
questions.explanation: "It’s useful, I can’t deny that … But I don’t enjoy it." Most fans "found us through videos online", and it is the bass player, not Jess, who "loves doing it".

questions.question: What does Jess like most about being in a band?
options: a) Playing at small, friendly gigs
b) Travelling to new places on tour
c) Playing in front of huge crowds
questions.explanation: "For me it’s the small gigs in tiny clubs, where you can see everyone’s faces". The big concerts are what "people expect me to say".

questions.question: What is Jess’s main advice for young musicians?
options: a) Practise alone in your bedroom every day.
b) Learn to play more than one instrument.
c) Play with others as often as you can.
questions.explanation: "More than that, play with other people as often as you can." Practising alone is not enough: "you only really improve when you have to listen to other musicians."

questions.question: Why has Joe written this note?
options: a) To tell the reader he is keeping a parcel for them
b) To ask the reader to take in a parcel for him
c) To complain about a delivery that went to the wrong flat
questions.explanation: Joe writes that "a parcel for you was left with me" and asks the reader to "knock after 6 pm to collect it". The parcel belongs to the person in Flat 6, not to Joe, and he does not complain – it was left with him "because you were out".

questions.question: What does the notice say?
options: a) Pushchairs must not be taken in the lift.
b) The caretaker is going to repair the lift.
c) Residents can get help carrying heavy things.
questions.explanation: Residents "with heavy shopping or pushchairs can ask the caretaker, Mr Patel, for help". The repair will be done by "An engineer", not the caretaker, and pushchairs are mentioned only because the lift is not working, not because they are banned.

questions.question: What does the notice tell residents?
options: a) Bikes that are not locked will be removed after 31 May.
b) They need to get a sticker for their bikes.
c) They must pay the office to keep their bikes here.
questions.explanation: "Any bike without a Brookfield House sticker will be removed", so residents need a sticker. The stickers "are free", so there is nothing to pay, and bikes are removed for having no sticker, not for being unlocked.

questions.question: What are residents advised to do?
options: a) Stay in their flats on Monday morning.
b) Keep some water ready for Monday.
c) Check their own pipes before 9 June.
questions.explanation: The email asks residents to "fill a few bottles the night before" the water is turned off. Nobody is asked to stay at home, and the company is replacing the pipes itself: "while old pipes are replaced".

questions.question: What is Lena doing?
options: a) Asking her neighbours to bring cake to a party
b) Asking permission to use the garden on Saturday
c) Inviting her neighbours to come and meet her
questions.explanation: Lena has "just moved into Flat 11" and is having a get-together "to say hello", so she is inviting neighbours to meet her. She is providing the "drinks and cake" herself, and she is not asking anyone for permission – she has already planned to use the garden or the entrance hall.

questions.question: Nadia has just left home and is learning to cook. She wants ideas for meals that don’t cost much, and she only has twenty minutes to listen on the bus.
options: A) The Long Lunch
B) Kitchen on a Budget
C) Slow English Travels
D) Run With Us
E) History Hour
F) Why Is the Sky Blue?
G) Body Matters
H) Voices from the Past
questions.explanation: Kitchen on a Budget shows "how to make a tasty dinner for two for under £5", and "Episodes last about fifteen minutes". The Long Lunch is also about food, but it is about restaurants, not cheap cooking, and "Episodes often last more than an hour".

questions.question: Kofi loves history, but he finds it boring when people just talk about it. He would prefer to hear stories from the past acted out.
options: A) The Long Lunch
B) Kitchen on a Budget
C) Slow English Travels
D) Run With Us
E) History Hour
F) Why Is the Sky Blue?
G) Body Matters
H) Voices from the Past
questions.explanation: In Voices from the Past "Actors bring real events from history to life", and each episode is "a short radio play". History Hour is also about history, but it is "Two university professors" in a "discussion", which is the kind of talk Kofi finds boring.

questions.question: Grace is preparing for her first 10-kilometre race. She wants something to listen to while she’s out running, with advice from other runners.
options: A) The Long Lunch
B) Kitchen on a Budget
C) Slow English Travels
D) Run With Us
E) History Hour
F) Why Is the Sky Blue?
G) Body Matters
H) Voices from the Past
questions.explanation: On Run With Us, runners "share their training tips", and each episode is planned "so you can listen with your headphones in while you’re out on the road". Body Matters talks about exercise, but it comes from a doctor, not runners, and is "best listened to at home".

questions.question: Leo wants a science podcast that he can listen to with his eleven-year-old son. They both enjoy things that make them laugh.
options: A) The Long Lunch
B) Kitchen on a Budget
C) Slow English Travels
D) Run With Us
E) History Hour
F) Why Is the Sky Blue?
G) Body Matters
H) Voices from the Past
questions.explanation: In Why Is the Sky Blue? two comedians question "a top scientist", "The jokes come thick and fast", and it is "suitable for the whole family". Body Matters also explains science, but it "is aimed at adults who want serious, reliable information".

questions.question: Mira is learning English and wants to practise her listening. She needs speakers who talk slowly, and she’d like to be able to read the words as well.
options: A) The Long Lunch
B) Kitchen on a Budget
C) Slow English Travels
D) Run With Us
E) History Hour
F) Why Is the Sky Blue?
G) Body Matters
H) Voices from the Past
questions.explanation: On Slow English Travels the presenter "speaks slowly and clearly", and "The full text of every episode can be downloaded free". The Long Lunch also has "a full written transcript", but the conversations are "lively and fast, with lots of jokes and people talking over each other".

questions.question: What did Ms Hughes think about the cardboard box?
options: a) It would not change habits on its own.
b) It just needed a little more time.
c) It needed a clearer sign on it.
d) It should be in a different place.
questions.explanation: Ms Hughes said: "People don’t change because of a box. They change because their friends do." She did not talk about the sign, the place or the time; her idea was that people follow their friends.

questions.question: What does Amara say was difficult about the film in assembly?
options: a) The younger students did not understand it.
b) Some older students made fun of the team.
c) Nobody wanted to join the team after seeing it.
d) It took the team a very long time to make.
questions.explanation: Amara writes: "some older ones laughed at us. That was hard." The younger students "loved it", and the volunteers joined the team before the film.

questions.question: How did the school get its recycling bins?
options: a) The head teacher paid for them from the school budget.
b) A local company gave them to the school for free.
c) The city council sent them after a letter from the team.
d) The students raised the money themselves.
questions.explanation: The team "organised a cake sale and a sponsored walk" which "raised £650, enough for ten bins." The head teacher had "no money", and the local company only empties the bins for free; it did not give them.

questions.question: What made the biggest difference to the number of plastic bottles?
options: a) The canteen stopped selling drinks in plastic.
b) Other schools in the city joined the project.
c) Students began to refill their own bottles.
d) The recycling bins were emptied more often.
questions.explanation: "The biggest change came from the water fountains": now "most students fill up their own bottle." The bins only "helped", and other schools asked for advice but did not join the project.

questions.question: What is Amara’s main point in the last paragraph?
options: a) Working with a team mattered more than the results.
b) Food waste will be easier to deal with than bottles.
c) The new figures prove the project was a success.
d) Being shy made it hard for her to lead the project.
questions.explanation: Amara says: "the people are more important than the numbers" and "Working with others gave me confidence." She says food waste "will be harder", and her shyness was not a problem because she had a team.

questions.question: Read the text "The Cornish pasty: a lunch with a handle". Which sentence (A–H) best fits gap 1?
questions.explanation: "These miners" refers to the "thousands of men" in the mines, and spending all day "deep underground, far away from their homes" explains why "They needed a meal that was filling, easy to carry". The sentence saying the pasty was too heavy to carry into the mines contradicts "The pasty was the perfect answer".
options: A) They took their love of pasties with them to their new homes.
B) Unfortunately, it was far too heavy to carry down into the mines.
C) These miners often spent the whole day deep underground, far away from their homes.
D) Most of them came back to Cornwall a few years later and never left again.
E) Wives sometimes marked each pasty with the initials of the man who was going to eat it.
F) Since then, most Cornish pasties have been made with chicken instead of beef.
G) This means that a pasty can only be called Cornish if it is prepared in Cornwall.
H) The two edges are then pressed together to make a thick crust called the crimp.

questions.question: Read the text "The Cornish pasty: a lunch with a handle". Which sentence (A–H) best fits gap 2?
