questions.explanation: "then" follows the description of the pastry "folded over a filling", and "a thick crust called the crimp" is what "this thick edge" in the next sentence refers to. The sentence about the pasty being too heavy cannot fit, because the text says it was "the perfect answer".
options: A) They took their love of pasties with them to their new homes.
B) Unfortunately, it was far too heavy to carry down into the mines.
C) These miners often spent the whole day deep underground, far away from their homes.
D) Most of them came back to Cornwall a few years later and never left again.
E) Wives sometimes marked each pasty with the initials of the man who was going to eat it.
F) Since then, most Cornish pasties have been made with chicken instead of beef.
G) This means that a pasty can only be called Cornish if it is prepared in Cornwall.
H) The two edges are then pressed together to make a thick crust called the crimp.

questions.question: Read the text "The Cornish pasty: a lunch with a handle". Which sentence (A–H) best fits gap 3?
questions.explanation: Marking each pasty with initials explains the next sentence: "That way, each man knew which pasty was his". The sentence about chicken instead of beef cannot fit, because nothing in it helps a man to know "which pasty was his".
options: A) They took their love of pasties with them to their new homes.
B) Unfortunately, it was far too heavy to carry down into the mines.
C) These miners often spent the whole day deep underground, far away from their homes.
D) Most of them came back to Cornwall a few years later and never left again.
E) Wives sometimes marked each pasty with the initials of the man who was going to eat it.
F) Since then, most Cornish pasties have been made with chicken instead of beef.
G) This means that a pasty can only be called Cornish if it is prepared in Cornwall.
H) The two edges are then pressed together to make a thick crust called the crimp.

questions.question: Read the text "The Cornish pasty: a lunch with a handle". Which sentence (A–H) best fits gap 4?
questions.explanation: "They" refers to the "Cornish miners" who "moved abroad", and taking pasties to their new homes explains why "you can still find pasties today in parts of Mexico, Australia and the United States". The sentence saying most of them came back to Cornwall is wrong, because then pasties would not have spread to those countries.
options: A) They took their love of pasties with them to their new homes.
B) Unfortunately, it was far too heavy to carry down into the mines.
C) These miners often spent the whole day deep underground, far away from their homes.
D) Most of them came back to Cornwall a few years later and never left again.
E) Wives sometimes marked each pasty with the initials of the man who was going to eat it.
F) Since then, most Cornish pasties have been made with chicken instead of beef.
G) This means that a pasty can only be called Cornish if it is prepared in Cornwall.
H) The two edges are then pressed together to make a thick crust called the crimp.

questions.question: Read the text "The Cornish pasty: a lunch with a handle". Which sentence (A–H) best fits gap 5?
questions.explanation: "This means" explains what the "special protection" is, and the next sentence adds a second rule: "It must also have the famous D shape". The sentence saying most pasties are now made with chicken is wrong, because it is not a rule and it does not prepare for "must also".
options: A) They took their love of pasties with them to their new homes.
B) Unfortunately, it was far too heavy to carry down into the mines.
C) These miners often spent the whole day deep underground, far away from their homes.
D) Most of them came back to Cornwall a few years later and never left again.
E) Wives sometimes marked each pasty with the initials of the man who was going to eat it.
F) Since then, most Cornish pasties have been made with chicken instead of beef.
G) This means that a pasty can only be called Cornish if it is prepared in Cornwall.
H) The two edges are then pressed together to make a thick crust called the crimp.

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits gap (1).
questions.explanation: Turn into means change from one thing to something different: the car park "turns into a lively flea market" every Sunday. None of the other three verbs is used with into to mean this kind of change.
options: a) becomes
b) gets
c) turns
d) makes

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits gap (2).
questions.explanation: A bargain is something bought for less than its real value: "you can often find a real bargain". You do not find a real offer, a real sale or a real price on a market table.
options: a) bargain
b) offer
c) sale
d) price

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits gap (3).
questions.explanation: Tom has a hobby: he "collects old cameras and already owns more than forty of them". Gathers is used for things lying around, saves for money, and picks for flowers or fruit, so none of them describes a collection.
options: a) gathers
b) saves
c) picks
d) collects

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits gap (4).
questions.explanation: Only expect follows the pattern verb + person + to-infinitive: "Sellers usually expect you to ask for a lower price". We cannot say hope you to, wait you to or insist you to.
options: a) insist
b) hope
c) expect
d) wait

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits gap (5).
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase for objects is in perfect condition: "a camera from the 1960s in perfect condition". In perfect form is used for athletes, in perfect health for people, and in perfect state is not used.
options: a) health
b) condition
c) state
d) form

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits gap (6).
questions.explanation: We spend money on something: "I just spent two pounds on a pile of old comics". Paid needs for, cost needs the thing as subject, and bought two pounds on is not possible.
options: a) cost
b) spent
c) bought
d) paid

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (1).
questions.explanation: Every single means all, one by one, and stresses how bad the results were: "they had lost every single match". This matches "a terrible reputation".

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (2).
questions.explanation: Teach someone how to do something describes a method: "teaching us how to pass the ball without looking at our feet". The words without looking describe the way of passing, so how is needed.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (3).
questions.explanation: Let someone down means disappoint them: "never to let the rest of the team down by missing training". No other particle gives this meaning.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (4).
questions.explanation: Even though means although, and makes the contrast stronger: nobody missed a session "even though the weather was often freezing". Only even goes before though here.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (5).
questions.explanation: The past continuous with we needs were: "At half-time we were losing 2–0". The story is in the past, so are is not possible.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (6).
questions.explanation: Each other shows that every player hugged the others: "we ran to hug each other". Only other completes the phrase.

questions.question:
Read this email from your English-speaking friend Callum and the notes you have made.

From: Callum
Subject: Clean-up day

Hi!
Our town is having a clean-up day on Saturday the 14th, and I’ve put both our names down as helpers! [Note 1: Fantastic!] Volunteers can clean the park, the river bank or the streets near the station. Which one shall we choose? [Note 2: Tell Callum] The organisers say we should bring some things with us, but they didn’t say what. What do you think we need? [Note 3: Suggest] Afterwards there’s a free picnic for all the helpers. Do you want to stay for it? [Note 4: No, because …]

See you,
Callum

Write your email to Callum using all the notes. Write about 100 words.
questions.explanation:
A good answer replies to all four notes: (1) says you are pleased Callum put your names down; (2) chooses the park, the river bank or the streets near the station, and gives a reason; (3) suggests what to bring, for example gloves, bags or old clothes; (4) explains why you cannot stay for the picnic. Use an informal greeting and ending, link your ideas and write about 100 words.

Model answer:
Hi Callum,
That’s fantastic – thanks for putting my name down! It’s a really good way to help our town.
Let’s choose the river bank. I walk my dog there every morning and there’s always lots of plastic in the water. It makes me sad.
I think we should bring strong gloves, some big rubbish bags and old clothes, because it might be muddy. A bottle of water is a good idea too.
Unfortunately I can’t stay for the picnic. It’s my grandad’s birthday that afternoon and we’re having lunch at his house.
See you on the 14th,
Lucía

questions.question:
Choose ONE of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

Question 2 – Article
You see this announcement in an English-language magazine for students.

Articles wanted!
HOW MY TOWN COULD BE GREENER
What is good about your town for the environment? What problems are there? What one change would make the biggest difference?
Write an article answering these questions. The best article will win a prize.

Write your article.

Question 3 – Story
Your English teacher has asked you to write a story.
Your story must begin with this sentence:
Nobody believed what we found in the river.

Write your story.
questions.explanation:
Article: give your article a title, answer all the questions in the announcement (what is good, what the problems are, one change you would make) and give reasons for your opinions. Story: begin with the given sentence, say what you found and how people reacted, and give the story a clear ending. Use past tenses consistently. In both tasks write about 100 words.

Model article:
A greener future for Westbridge
My town already does some things well. There are recycling bins on every street, and the old factory has become a lovely park.
However, there are still problems. The centre is full of cars, especially in the morning, and the air can be quite dirty. There also aren’t enough safe places to ride a bike.
If I could change one thing, I would close the main street to traffic and plant trees there. People could walk, cycle and meet their friends outside. Wouldn’t that be better for everyone?

Model story:
Nobody believed what we found in the river. It was during a school project, and my friend Sam and I were collecting rubbish near the old bridge.
Suddenly Sam pulled out a heavy metal box. Inside there were old coins and a letter dated 1923. We took everything to the town museum.
At first the staff thought it was a joke, but after a few days they called our school. The coins were real, and the letter had belonged to a local family.
Now our box is in the museum, with our names next to it!

questions.question:
Part 1 – Interview
The examiner asks you some questions about yourself. Answer each question and give some extra information.

Have you got a pet, or did you have one when you were younger?
What is your favourite animal? Why?
Do any of your friends or relatives have pets?
Have you ever been to a zoo or a farm? What did you see there?
Would you like to have a pet in the future? Which one?
questions.explanation:
Give full answers: answer the question, then add a reason or an example. Use the present perfect with ever, the past simple for finished experiences and would like for the future.

Model answers:
Yes, we’ve got a cat called Biscuit. We’ve had her for six years, and she sleeps on my bed every night.
My favourite animal is the elephant. Elephants are really intelligent, and they look after each other in their family groups.
My best friend has two rabbits. They live in a big cage in the garden, and I sometimes help her feed them.
Yes, I went to a farm with my school last spring. We saw cows, sheep and some baby goats, and we were allowed to feed them.
I’d love to have a dog one day, maybe when I have my own flat with a garden.

questions.question:
Part 2 – Photo description
Look at the photograph. It shows a girl walking five dogs along a path in a park. She is holding all the leads in one hand. The dogs are different sizes: two of them are large and three are small, and one of the small dogs is white with brown spots. The girl is wearing a red jacket and trainers. There are tall trees and green grass on both sides of the path, and a man is jogging in the background. Tell us what you can see in the photograph.

Talk for about one minute.
questions.explanation:
Describe the place, the people, the animals and what is happening, using the present continuous (is walking, is jogging). Talk about details such as colours and sizes, and say where things are (on both sides of, in the background). If you do not know a word, explain it in other words, for example the long thing you use to hold a dog. Only describe what is in the photo; do not invent new details.

Model answer:
In this photo I can see a girl in a park. She’s walking five dogs along a path. She’s holding all the leads in one hand, which must be quite difficult! The dogs are different sizes – two of them are large and three are small. One of the small ones is white with brown spots. The girl is wearing a red jacket and trainers. On both sides of the path there are tall trees and green grass, and in the background there’s a man who is jogging. It looks like a nice, quiet place for a walk.

questions.question:
Part 3 – Collaborative task
A family would like to have a pet, but both parents work full-time and the children are at school all day. Here are some pets they are thinking about.

a dog
a cat
a goldfish
a rabbit
a hamster
a parrot

Talk together about the good and bad points of each pet for a busy family. Then decide which pet would be the best for them.

Talk together for about two or three minutes.
questions.explanation:
Discuss the pets one by one and give reasons, thinking about the family’s situation (time, space, cost). Ask your partner what they think, agree and disagree politely, and make a decision together at the end. Useful language: The problem with … is that … On the other hand … I think … would be easier to look after. So we agree that …?

Model conversation (part):
A: A dog would be fun, but it needs a walk every day, and it would be alone all day.
B: I agree, that wouldn’t be fair on the dog. What about a cat? Cats are quite independent.
A: Yes, they can stay at home alone, and they don’t need walks. But they can damage furniture.
B: True. A goldfish is the easiest, but the children can’t really play with it.
A: And a parrot can be very noisy, and some parrots live for fifty years!
B: Really? Then I think the cat is the best choice. It’s friendly but doesn’t need too much time.
A: OK, let’s choose the cat.

questions.question:
Part 4 – General conversation
The examiner asks you and your partner some questions about people and animals. Give your opinion and talk to your partner too.

Why do you think so many people have pets?
What can children learn from looking after an animal?
Do you think animals should live in zoos? Why or why not?
Are pets popular in your country? Which ones?
Would you like to have a job working with animals?
questions.explanation:
Give your opinion with a reason or an example, and react to your partner (I agree with you; That’s true, but …). Use would for the question about a job.

Model answers:
I think pets make people happy. They’re good company, especially for people who live alone.
They learn to be responsible, because they have to feed the animal and keep its home clean every day.
I’m not sure. Good zoos help to protect animals that are in danger, but I feel sorry for big animals like lions in small spaces.
Yes, very. Dogs and cats are the most popular, but lots of children have hamsters or fish too.
Maybe. I’d like to work as a vet, but I think it would be very sad when an animal is ill and you can’t help it.

passages.title: Recording 1
passages.text: Woman: Are you coming to the shopping centre later? Man: I'd love to, but I have to finish my history project first. Maybe I can meet you there at five o'clock instead?

passages.title: Recording 2
passages.text: Boy: I need to buy a new pair of trainers for the school trip. Do you think these blue ones look okay? Girl: They look cool, but they are quite expensive. Why don't you check the ones on sale?

passages.title: Recording 3
passages.text: Woman: Have you decided what to wear for the party on Saturday? Man: I was going to wear my suit, but it needs cleaning. I think I'll just wear my new jeans and a shirt.

passages.title: Recording 4
passages.text: Man: I'm planning to go to the cinema this evening. Would you like to come? Woman: That sounds great! I've been wanting to see that new comedy film for ages.

passages.title: Recording 5
passages.text: Girl: I'm going to the supermarket to get some snacks for our picnic tomorrow. Do you want anything specific? Boy: Could you get some apples and maybe some orange juice?

passages.title: Recording 6
passages.text: Woman: I've finally finished my shopping for the holiday. I bought a new swimsuit and a sun hat. Man: That's good! I still need to find some comfortable sandals.

passages.title: Recording 7
passages.text: Man: What time are we meeting for the concert? Woman: The doors open at seven, so let's meet outside the main entrance at half past six.

passages.title: Recording 1

passages.title: Recording 2
passages.text: Girl: Did you see the new market in the town square? They sell amazing handmade jewellery. Boy: Yes, I went yesterday! I bought a gift for my sister's birthday. It was quite expensive, but worth it.

passages.title: Recording 3
passages.text: Man: I'm planning to go hiking this weekend if the weather is nice. Would you like to come? Woman: That sounds great, but I've already promised to help my brother move house on Saturday morning.

passages.title: Recording 4
passages.text: Woman: I've been looking for a blue dress for the party, but all the shops are sold out of my size. Man: Have you checked the online store? They usually have more stock than the physical shop.

passages.title: Recording 5
passages.text: Boy: We need to decide what to do for Sarah's surprise party. Should we order pizza or cook something ourselves? Girl: Let's order pizza. It's much easier and we won't have to clean up the kitchen afterwards.

passages.title: Recording 6
passages.text: Man: I'm really looking forward to the cinema trip on Friday. What time does the film start? Woman: It starts at 7:30, so let's meet outside the entrance at 7:15 to get some popcorn.

passages.title: Recording 7
passages.text: Woman: I've decided to start a photography course next month. Man: That's a brilliant idea! You've always been good at taking pictures. Will it be on weekends or during the week?

passages.title: Recording 2
passages.text: Man: Did you see the weather report for the coast this weekend? Woman: Yes, it looks like there will be plenty of sunshine, so we should definitely take the boat out on Sunday.

passages.title: Recording 3
passages.text: Woman: I'm so disappointed. We were going to have the picnic in the park, but now they are predicting thunderstorms all afternoon.

passages.title: Recording 4
passages.text: Man: It's freezing outside today! I hope the snow melts by Saturday so we can drive to the mountains for the ski trip.

passages.title: Recording 5
passages.text: Woman: Shall we go to the beach? Man: Well, it's quite cloudy right now, but the news says it will clear up by midday, so let's go later.

passages.title: Recording 6
passages.text: Man: I've been waiting for a warm weekend to paint the garden fence. It looks like Saturday will be perfect, just warm and dry.

passages.title: Recording 7
passages.text: Woman: The weather is so unpredictable lately. One minute it's sunny, the next it's hailing. I think we should just stay home and watch a movie.

passages.title: Dialogue 1: Weekend Trip
passages.text: Woman: Are we still going to the coast on Saturday? Man: I'm afraid not. My brother is visiting, so we're going to have a big family lunch at home instead. Woman: Oh, that sounds nice anyway.

passages.title: Dialogue 2: Birthday Party
passages.text: Boy: Have you finished the invitations for your sister's party? Girl: Almost. I just need to add the time. My mum said we should start at four, but I think five is better so everyone can get there after work.

passages.title: Dialogue 3: School Project
passages.text: Man: Did you manage to help your cousin with his history project? Woman: Yes, we spent all evening looking at old family photos. It was actually quite interesting to see how much the house has changed.

passages.title: Dialogue 4: Moving House
passages.text: Woman: Are you ready for the move next week? Man: Not really. My uncle is coming to help us pack the boxes, but there is just so much stuff to sort through before then.

passages.title: Dialogue 5: Cinema Visit
passages.text: Boy: Shall we go to the cinema on Sunday? Girl: I can't. My aunt is taking the whole family to the theatre to see that new musical. Maybe we can go next week?

passages.title: Dialogue 6: Camping Trip
passages.text: Man: Is your family still planning to go camping in July? Woman: We were, but my grandmother is not feeling very well, so we've decided to stay at home and visit her instead.

passages.title: Dialogue 1
passages.text: Woman: Are you coming to the climbing wall tonight? Man: I'd love to, but I've already promised to help my brother move house. Maybe next week?

passages.title: Dialogue 2
passages.text: Boy: Did you finish that book I lent you? Girl: Not yet, I've been so busy with my guitar lessons that I've only managed to read a few pages.

passages.title: Dialogue 3
passages.text: Man: The weather is perfect for a bike ride today. Woman: I agree, but I think I'll go to the gym instead. I need to get ready for the marathon.

passages.title: Dialogue 4
passages.text: Girl: Are you going to the art exhibition this weekend? Boy: I was planning to, but the tickets are sold out. I'll probably just stay home and paint.

passages.title: Dialogue 5
passages.text: Woman: Do you want to join the chess club? Man: I'm not really into board games. I prefer spending my time outdoors, like hiking or swimming.

passages.title: Dialogue 6
passages.text: Boy: I've finally finished my painting! Girl: That's great! Does that mean you're free to come to the cinema with us later?

passages.title: Dialogue 1
passages.text: Woman: I've finally booked our trip to Spain for July! Man: That's great, but isn't it going to be extremely hot? Woman: I know, but we'll be right by the sea, so we can swim all day.

passages.title: Dialogue 2
passages.text: Man: Did you manage to pack everything for the camping trip? Woman: Almost, but I can't find the tent pegs. Man: Don't worry, I think I left them in the garage last time we went away.

passages.title: Dialogue 3
passages.text: Woman: I'm really looking forward to the city break, but I'm worried about the flight times. Man: Why? Woman: We have to be at the airport at 4 a.m. for the early departure.

passages.title: Dialogue 4
passages.text: Man: Should we take the train or drive to the coast? Woman: The train is much faster and we won't have to worry about finding a parking space in the busy town center.

passages.title: Dialogue 5
passages.text: Woman: Have you checked the weather forecast for our hiking trip? Man: Yes, it says it will be cloudy but dry, so we should be fine as long as we have warm jackets.

passages.title: Dialogue 6
passages.text: Man: I think we should stay in a hotel rather than a hostel this time. Woman: I agree, it's our anniversary, so let's treat ourselves to something a bit more comfortable.

passages.title: New Library Services
passages.text: Hello everyone. I am here to tell you about the exciting changes coming to our local library next month. First, we are introducing a new online reservation system. You will be able to book books from home using your library card number. We are also opening a new study area on the second floor, which will be equipped with ten high-speed computers. For those who enjoy reading outside, we are launching a 'Books in the Park' scheme where you can borrow items from a mobile stand near the fountain. Please note that the library will be closed for renovations on the 15th of July. If you need help with your digital skills, we are starting free weekly workshops every Wednesday morning. Finally, if you have any suggestions, please leave a note in the suggestion box located next to the main entrance.

passages.title: School Trip to France
passages.text: Hello everyone. I am here to give you the final details about our upcoming school trip to France. We will be departing from the school gates at 7:30 am on Monday morning, so please make sure you arrive on time. We are staying at a lovely hotel in the countryside, which is famous for its large swimming pool. On the first day, we will visit a local museum to learn about history. The most exciting part of the trip will be the visit to the chocolate factory on Wednesday, where we can taste everything! For lunch, we will have a picnic in the park, but please remember to bring a bottle of water. Finally, don't forget to bring your camera to take photos of the beautiful scenery. I am sure we will have a fantastic time!

passages.title: New Sports Centre Opening
passages.text: Hello everyone! I am delighted to announce that the Riverside Sports Centre will finally open its doors to the public next Monday. We have spent months preparing the facilities. If you are interested in swimming, our main pool is 25 metres long and has a special area for children. For those who prefer fitness, the gym is equipped with the latest machines, and we offer a variety of classes including yoga and aerobics. We are currently looking for a receptionist to join our team, so please check our website if you are interested. Membership fees are very reasonable, and if you sign up before the end of the month, you will receive a discount of 15 percent on your first year. We also have a cafe on the ground floor where you can relax after your workout. We look forward to seeing you there!

passages.title: Interview with a Game Designer
passages.text: Interviewer: Today we are talking to Sarah Jenkins, who designs video games for a living. Sarah, was it always your dream to work in this industry? Sarah: Actually, no. I studied architecture at university. I loved drawing buildings, but I found the work a bit slow. One day, a friend showed me how to code a simple game, and I was hooked. I realized that game design is like architecture, but you can build entire worlds that people can interact with. Interviewer: That sounds fascinating. What is the most challenging part of your job? Sarah: People think it is just playing games all day, but it is actually very stressful. We have strict deadlines. If the game isn't ready for the holiday season, the company loses a lot of money. Sometimes I spend 12 hours a day staring at code. Interviewer: Do you ever get tired of it? Sarah: Sometimes, but then I see someone playing a game I helped create, and their face lights up. That feeling is worth all the hard work. Interviewer: What advice would you give to young people wanting to enter the field? Sarah: Don't just play games—learn how they are made. Start with simple tools and don't be afraid to make mistakes. Your first game will probably be terrible, and that is perfectly fine!

passages.title: Interview with Travel Blogger Sarah Jenkins
passages.text: Interviewer: Sarah, you've been blogging for five years now. What made you start? Sarah: I was working in an office and felt bored. I took a trip to Peru and realized I wanted to share my experiences. Interviewer: Was it hard to get started? Sarah: Yes, I didn't know anything about photography or writing for an audience. I had to learn everything from scratch. Interviewer: Many people think travel blogging is just a holiday. What do you say to them? Sarah: It's definitely not! I spend hours editing photos and researching locations. It's a full-time job. Interviewer: Do you ever get lonely? Sarah: Sometimes, but I meet so many interesting people on the road that it balances out. Interviewer: What is your favorite part of the job? Sarah: Seeing a place I've only read about in books. It's magical. Interviewer: Any advice for beginners? Sarah: Be yourself. Don't try to copy other bloggers. Authenticity is what people want to see.

passages.title: Interview with a young chef
passages.text: Interviewer: Today we are joined by Maya, a 22-year-old chef who recently opened her first restaurant. Maya, was it always your dream to cook professionally? Maya: Honestly, no. I studied graphic design first! But I spent all my free time helping my grandmother in her kitchen. I realized that the pressure of a busy service was actually where I felt most alive. Interviewer: Many people find the long hours in a kitchen difficult. How do you manage? Maya: It is exhausting, I won't lie. You are on your feet for twelve hours. But I have a great team, and we support each other. If I didn't love the creativity of inventing new dishes, I would have quit months ago. Interviewer: What is the most challenging part of your job? Maya: People think it's the cooking, but it's actually the management. Ordering ingredients, dealing with staff, and keeping the budget in check—that's the real work. The cooking is the reward at the end of the day. Interviewer: Do you have advice for young people wanting to enter the industry? Maya: Don't expect to be a head chef immediately. Start at the bottom, learn how to clean, how to prep, and be humble. You need to be willing to fail a few times before you get it right.

passages.title: Interview with a young chef
passages.text: Interviewer: Today we are talking to Sarah Jenkins, who recently opened her own restaurant at just twenty-two. Sarah, was it always your dream to be a chef? Sarah: Actually, no. I wanted to be a musician, but I loved cooking for friends. Then, I took a summer job in a kitchen and realized I preferred the heat of the stove to the stage! Interviewer: Was it difficult to start your own business so young? Sarah: The hardest part wasn't the cooking, but the paperwork. I spent weeks talking to banks and finding the right location. I almost gave up once, but my mentor encouraged me to keep going. Interviewer: What is the most popular dish on your menu? Sarah: Definitely the spicy vegetable stew. I thought people would find it too hot, but they love it. I use a secret spice mix from my grandmother. Interviewer: What do you do when you are not working? Sarah: I try to get away from food entirely! I go hiking or read books. If I stay in the kitchen too long, I lose my creativity. Interviewer: What advice would you give to other young people? Sarah: Don't be afraid to make mistakes. Every burnt meal is a lesson.

C) City History Museum: Learn about the town's industrial past. Guided tours are available every hour. Perfect for rainy days.
D) Seaside Aquarium: Discover marine life from across the globe. Interactive touch pools are open for children in the afternoons.
E) Forest Botanical Gardens: A peaceful escape featuring rare flowers and quiet walking paths. Ideal for those interested in photography.

passages.text: Explore ancient artifacts and learn about the city's origins. The museum features interactive displays that are great for families with children who want to learn while having fun.

passages.title: H: Lakeside Boat Rentals
passages.text: Rent a small rowing boat or a pedal boat for an hour or two. It is a fun way to get out on the water and enjoy the sunshine with friends or family.

passages.text: Visit our vibrant market to find unique handmade crafts, vintage clothing, and delicious street food from around the world. It is open every Saturday and Sunday.

passages.title: D: City Art Gallery
passages.text: A quiet place to spend an afternoon. The gallery displays modern art from local artists and hosts weekly workshops where you can learn to paint or sculpt yourself.

passages.title: A New Beginning
passages.text:
Moving to a new city is often described as an exciting adventure, but for me, it felt more like a challenge I wasn't ready for. Last summer, my parents announced that we were moving from our quiet village to the bustling city of Manchester. I had lived in the same house for fourteen years, and the thought of leaving my friends and my favourite local park was devastating.

When we first arrived, the noise was the biggest shock. Unlike the peaceful nights I was used to, the city never seemed to sleep. There were sirens, traffic, and people talking at all hours. For the first two weeks, I barely left my room. I felt like an outsider looking in, convinced that I would never fit into this fast-paced environment. I spent most of my time messaging my old friends, feeling sorry for myself.

However, everything changed when I joined a local photography club. I had always enjoyed taking pictures, and I thought it might be a good way to get out of the house. On my first day, I met a girl named Sarah who was also new to the area. We started exploring the city together, looking for interesting buildings and street art to photograph. Through her eyes, I began to see the city differently. Instead of just seeing traffic and noise, I started to notice the beautiful architecture and the vibrant culture.

It has been six months now, and I can honestly say I don't regret the move. While I still miss my old friends, I have built a new life here. I have learned that moving isn't just about changing your address; it is about changing your perspective. You have to be willing to step outside your comfort zone to find the hidden gems in any new place. If you are facing a big move, my advice is to find a hobby or a group that shares your interests. It makes the world feel a lot smaller and much friendlier.

passages.title: A Life-Changing Summer in Peru
passages.text: Last summer, I decided to do something completely different. Instead of spending my holidays at home, I signed up for a volunteer program in a small village in the Peruvian Andes. I had always wanted to travel, but I wanted to do more than just visit tourist sites; I wanted to make a real difference. When I arrived, I was surprised by how different everything was. The air was thin, the mountains were breathtaking, and the local community was incredibly welcoming. My main job was to help build a new classroom for the primary school. I had never held a hammer or painted a wall before, but the local builders were very patient with me. They taught me how to mix cement and how to work as part of a team. It was hard physical work, especially in the heat, but I felt a great sense of achievement every evening. In the afternoons, I helped the children with their English homework. They were so eager to learn, and we often spent hours laughing as we tried to communicate through gestures and simple words. Living without electricity and limited internet access was a challenge at first. I missed my friends and the comforts of home, but as the weeks passed, I realized that I didn't need those things to be happy. I learned to appreciate the simple things, like a shared meal or a beautiful sunset over the peaks. This experience changed my perspective on life. I realized that we don't need much to be happy, and that helping others is one of the most rewarding things you can do. I returned home with a new sense of purpose and a promise to myself that I would continue volunteering in the future. I have already started looking for local opportunities in my own city.

passages.title: Rising Star: An Interview with Leo Vance
passages.text:
At just sixteen, Leo Vance has already made a name for himself in the world of competitive swimming. We caught up with him at his local training centre in Manchester. 'I started swimming when I was five,' Leo explains, drying off after a two-hour morning session. 'My parents took me to the pool every weekend, but I didn't really take it seriously until I joined a club at ten.'

Leo’s routine is demanding. He wakes up at 4:30 a.m. to be in the water by 5:15 a.m. 'It’s tough, especially in winter when it's dark and cold outside,' he admits. 'But when you’re in the pool, you forget the time. You just focus on your strokes.' Despite the hard work, Leo insists he has a normal social life. 'People think athletes don't have time for friends, but I make sure I see my mates on Friday nights. It’s important to switch off.'

His biggest challenge so far was the National Youth Championships last year. 'I was so nervous before the final race,' he recalls. 'I almost pulled out, but my coach reminded me why I started. I ended up winning silver.' That medal changed his perspective. 'It wasn't just about the prize; it was about proving to myself that I could handle the pressure.'

Looking ahead, Leo has his sights set on the international stage. 'The dream is the Olympics, obviously. But for now, I’m focused on improving my technique. My coach says I’m strong, but my turns need work.' When asked if he has any advice for other young athletes, he is humble. 'Don't let the sport define who you are. Enjoy it, work hard, but remember to have fun. If you stop enjoying it, you’ll never reach your potential.'

passages.title: The Green Revolution in Cities
passages.text:
Modern cities are undergoing a significant transformation as urban planners prioritize the creation of green spaces. For many years, concrete and glass dominated the skyline, but now the focus is shifting towards parks and gardens. (1) ________. These areas act as the lungs of the city, filtering pollutants and providing a necessary escape from the noise of traffic. 

Research has shown that access to nature significantly improves the mental health of residents. (2) ________. Consequently, city councils are investing millions into converting unused industrial land into public parks. Some of these projects are quite ambitious, involving the planting of thousands of native trees and the creation of artificial lakes. (3) ________. 

However, maintaining these spaces requires careful planning and constant funding. It is not enough to simply plant grass and trees; the city must ensure that these areas remain safe and accessible for everyone. (4) ________. This includes installing proper lighting and creating well-maintained paths for walkers and cyclists. 

Ultimately, the goal is to create a sustainable urban environment where people and nature can coexist. (5) ________. By making cities greener, we are not only improving our quality of life today but also ensuring a healthier future for the next generation.

The owner was very kind and let me taste three different types before I made my choice. After buying a jar of honey, I felt hungry and looked for something to eat. (3) __________ It was filled with fresh herbs and local vegetables. It was probably the best lunch I have had in a long time. While I was eating, a local band started playing some relaxing music near the fountain. (4) __________ Many families were sitting on the grass, enjoying the sunshine and the music. It was a perfect way to spend a Saturday morning. I will definitely return next weekend to try some of the other delicious treats. passages.title: Meeting Time
passages.text:
[Man]: Hi Sarah, are we still meeting at quarter past five?
[Woman]: Well, my class doesn't finish until five o'clock, and it takes me half an hour to get to the café. Can we make it quarter to six instead?
[Man]: That's a bit late because the film starts at six. Let's say half past five.
[Woman]: Okay, see you then.

passages.title: Buying a Bag
passages.text:
[Woman]: Look at my new bag! I wanted a small round one, but when I got to the shop, I saw this square leather one and fell in love with it.
[Man]: It's nice. I thought you were looking for one with long straps to wear over your shoulder?
[Woman]: I was, but this one has short handles and it's actually much easier to carry.

passages.title: Lunch Plans
passages.text:
[Man]: Shall we go to that new Italian restaurant by the river for lunch?
[Woman]: I'd love to, but it's always so busy. Why don't we just get some sandwiches and sit in the park? It's really sunny today.
[Man]: Actually, I heard there's a lovely café inside the museum that has outdoor seating. It's quiet too.
[Woman]: Oh, that sounds perfect. Let's go there.

passages.title: Birthday Present
passages.text:
[Man]: I need to get a birthday present for my sister. I was thinking of a silver necklace.
[Woman]: She doesn't really wear jewelry, does she? What about that book she wanted?
[Man]: Our parents already bought her that. I think I'll get her a nice wool scarf instead. It's getting cold now.
[Woman]: That's a lovely idea.

passages.title: Lost Keys
passages.text:
[Man]: I can't find my keys anywhere! I thought I left them on the kitchen table next to my wallet.
[Woman]: Did you check your coat pocket? You had them when we came inside.
[Man]: Yes, I checked. Oh, wait, I remember now. I put them down on the shelf by the front door when I was taking off my shoes.
[Woman]: Ah, yes, there they are!

passages.title: Weather Forecast
passages.text: [Presenter]: Here is the weather forecast for tomorrow. It will be a very wet start to the day, with heavy rain during the morning. However, by lunchtime, the rain will clear up, leaving us with cloudy but dry skies for the rest of the afternoon. We might even see some sunshine by the evening.

passages.title: Jack's Sport
passages.text:
[Woman]: Did you go to the indoor climbing wall yesterday, Jack?
[Man]: I wanted to, but it was fully booked. My brother suggested going for a bike ride instead, but then his bicycle had a flat tire. So we ended up playing tennis at the local club.
[Woman]: At least you did some exercise!

passages.title: Dialogue 1: Photography
passages.text:
Woman: Did you see the photos I posted from my weekend walk?
Man: Yes, they're amazing! The lighting in the forest was perfect. I didn't know you were so good at photography.
Woman: Thanks! I've been practicing a lot, but I still struggle with getting the focus right on moving objects, like birds.
Man: Well, you've definitely got a talent for landscapes.

passages.title: Dialogue 2: Hiking
passages.text:
Man: Are you coming hiking with us on Sunday? We're going up to the peak.
Woman: I'd love to, but my hiking boots are completely worn out, and I haven't had time to buy new ones.
Man: You could just wear your running trainers. The path is quite flat until the very end.
Woman: Actually, the weather forecast says it's going to rain, so the ground will be too muddy for trainers. I'll pass this time.

passages.title: Dialogue 3: Board Games
passages.text:
Woman: Have you played that new strategy board game yet?
Man: Yes, my brother bought it. It took us about an hour just to read the instructions!
Woman: I know, it's really complicated at first. But once you get started, it's incredibly fun.
Man: Definitely. We ended up playing until midnight. I can't wait to play it again this weekend.

passages.title: Dialogue 4: Cooking Class
passages.text:
Man: How was your first Italian cooking class yesterday?
Woman: It was great! The chef was really funny and explained everything clearly.
Man: Did you make pasta from scratch?
Woman: Yes, though mine turned out a bit too thick. Still, it tasted amazing, and I learned some useful techniques that I can easily try at home.

passages.title: Dialogue 5: Cinema
passages.text:
Woman: Do you want to see the new science-fiction film tonight?
Man: I've heard the special effects are incredible, but the story is quite weak and predictable.
Woman: Really? The reviews I read said the acting was brilliant, especially the main character.
Man: Well, I suppose we should judge for ourselves. Let's get tickets.

passages.title: Dialogue 6: Guitar Practice
passages.text:
Man: I'm thinking of giving up the guitar. I've been practicing for three months and I still can't play a whole song.
Woman: Don't be so hard on yourself! It takes time. Are you practicing every day?
Man: Well, only on weekends, really. I'm too tired after work.
Woman: That's the problem. Even fifteen minutes a day during the week would make a huge difference.

passages.title: Photography Talk
passages.text:
Boy: Did you see the photos I took at the park yesterday?
Girl: Yes, they're really good! The lighting on the lake was perfect. But why didn't you get closer to the birds? They look a bit small.
Boy: I know, but I didn't want to scare them away. Next time I'll use a better zoom lens.
Girl: Good idea. Still, you've got a real talent for finding great angles.

passages.title: Weekend Hiking Plans
passages.text:
Girl: Are you coming on the mountain hike this weekend?
Boy: I'd love to, but my boots are completely worn out. I need to buy a new pair before I do any serious climbing.
Girl: You could always borrow my brother's. He's got some spares.
Boy: Thanks, but hiking boots need to fit perfectly, otherwise you get terrible blisters. I'll just go shopping on Saturday instead.

passages.title: Playing a Board Game
passages.text:
Girl: That new board game we played last night was so complicated!
Boy: Really? I thought the rules were quite straightforward once we started.
Girl: Easy for you to say! You won! I spent half the time trying to figure out what my cards meant.
Boy: Well, it does take a couple of rounds to get used to it. Let's play again tonight and I'll help you.

passages.title: Guitar Practice
passages.text:
Boy: How are your guitar lessons going?
Girl: Okay, I suppose. My teacher wants me to practice classical music, but I really want to learn rock songs.
Boy: Classical is great for your technique, though. It makes your fingers much stronger.
Girl: I know, and I can feel the difference already. It's just not as fun as playing my favorite bands' tracks.

passages.title: Italian Cooking Class
passages.text:
Girl: How was the Italian cooking class yesterday?
Boy: Great! We made fresh pasta from scratch. It was much easier than I thought it would be.
Girl: Really? I always thought you needed special machines for that.
Boy: We just used a rolling pin and a knife. The chef was brilliant at explaining each step. I can't wait to try making it at home for my family.

passages.title: Watching a Sci-Fi Film
passages.text:
Boy: Did you watch that new sci-fi film last night?
Girl: Yes, I did. The special effects were absolutely amazing, especially the space battles.
Boy: Definitely. But I felt the story was a bit weak. It was just like every other space movie.
Girl: I agree. You could guess the ending after the first twenty minutes. But it was still highly entertaining.

passages.title: Information about a Museum Visit
passages.text:
Hello everyone, and welcome to our school trip to the Science Museum. Before we go inside, I have some important information for you, so please listen carefully and write down these details on your worksheets.

First, we are very lucky because there is a special exhibition on at the moment. It is called 'Robots', and it shows how machines have changed over the last hundred years. This exhibition has been very popular, and it is actually ending next month, on the twelfth of October, so make sure you don't miss it today.

Now, a little bit of history. The museum is quite old. It was first opened to the public in 1925, and it has grown a lot since then.

There are many amazing things to see, but the most popular object in the whole museum is a large model of a spaceship. You can find it in the transport gallery on the second floor.

After your tour, you might want to visit the museum shop. They have some great souvenirs. You can get books and keyrings, but the shop is currently offering a discount on posters, which are very cheap today.

Finally, about our travel arrangements. We need to meet back at the main entrance at four o'clock. The bus back to school will leave at 4.30 exactly. Please do not be late, as the driver cannot wait. Enjoy your visit!

passages.title: Information about a Museum Visit
passages.text:
Hello everyone, and thank you for joining our tour group today. I want to give you some practical information about our visit to the Science Museum tomorrow.

First, we will meet outside the main entrance at 8.45 am. Please don't be late as the bus leaves at exactly nine o'clock.

When we arrive, we will start our visit in the transport gallery on the ground floor. This is always very popular because of the old steam trains.

After that, you will have some free time. I highly recommend visiting the special exhibition on the first floor. It is about robots and how they are used in everyday life.

For lunch, you can eat your own sandwiches in the picnic area, which is next to the museum shop. Please do not eat inside the exhibition rooms.

In the afternoon, we have booked a special 3D film in the IMAX cinema. The film is about the history of space exploration. It starts at two-thirty and lasts for forty minutes.

Finally, before we go home, you can visit the gift shop. If you show your group ticket, you can get a discount on books and posters.

Are there any questions?

passages.title: Interview with a Travel Blogger
passages.text:
Interviewer: Today I'm talking to Elena Rossi, a successful travel blogger. Elena, welcome. Why did you first start your blog, 'Elena's Footsteps'?

Elena: Well, I didn't plan to make it my job! I actually started it when I went on a gap year to South America. My parents were really worried, so I promised to write regular updates so they'd know I was safe. I didn't think anyone else would read it, but then other travelers started finding my posts and asking for advice.

Interviewer: That's amazing. You've been to so many countries. Which one stands out the most?

Elena: People always ask this! I love Japan for its food, and Iceland for the landscapes, but my absolute favorite was Albania. I didn't know much about it before going, but the local people were incredibly welcoming. One family even invited me into their home for dinner when I got lost. That kindness is what I remember most.

Interviewer: Traveling isn't always easy, though. How do you deal with things when they go wrong?

Elena: Oh, I've had missed flights, lost luggage, and food poisoning! At first, I used to get really stressed and angry. But I quickly realized that doesn't help. Now, I just accept that problems are part of the adventure. I try to stay calm and look for a solution, often by asking locals. They are usually happy to help a confused tourist.

Interviewer: You usually travel by yourself. Do you prefer that?

Elena: I do. When you travel with friends, you tend to stay in your own little bubble. But when you're on your own, you're forced to talk to strangers, which means you make new friends much faster. Of course, it can be lonely occasionally, but the freedom to decide where to go next without arguing is worth it.

Interviewer: What's the most challenging part of being a professional blogger?

Elena: People think it's a permanent holiday, but it's hard work. The toughest thing for me is the lack of a routine. I'm constantly moving, which makes it hard to exercise regularly or eat healthily. I don't mind the long hours spent editing photos or writing posts, because I love doing that, but not having a proper home base can be exhausting.

Interviewer: Finally, what tips do you have for someone wanting to start a travel blog?

Elena: Don't just write about the famous tourist spots that everyone knows. Try to find a unique angle. Write about your personal feelings and the small details, like the smell of a local market. And most importantly, write because you love it, not because you want to get free hotel rooms. Readers can tell if you aren't being genuine.

Interviewer: Thank you, Elena!

passages.title: Great Day Trips in the Region
passages.text:
A. Highwood House
Step back in time at this stunning 18th-century manor. Explore the beautifully landscaped gardens and take a guided tour of the historic rooms. Tickets are quite pricey, and because of its remote countryside location, there is no public transport, so you will need to drive.

B. The Reedlands
This peaceful nature Reserve is a paradise for bird watchers and wildlife lovers. Take a relaxing boat trip along the river for a very low price. The Reserve is located right next to a train station, making it easy to reach. There is a small cafe on board, though there are no shops here.

C. Peak Heights
For those who love being active, a trip up the mountain is a must. Enjoy challenging hiking trails or take the cable car to the summit for breathtaking views. There is an excellent souvenir shop and a cafe at the top. It is expensive and only accessible by car.

D. Seabreeze Cove
Spend a relaxing day at this beautiful coastal village. Walk along the sandy beach, taste fresh local seafood at the harbor restaurants, and browse the small local art galleries. A regular bus service runs from the city center, and it is very budget-friendly.

E. Deep Stone Caves
Discover amazing rock formations on a fascinating guided underground tour of these ancient caves. It is cool inside, so bring a jacket! A Bus stop is located just outside the entrance. There is a great gift shop selling unique local stone crafts. Booking in advance is recommended.

F. Greenwood Park
Get your adrenaline pumping with a tree-top canopy walk and adventure sports in this deep forest. It is a fantastic day out for active people, though entry fees are high. You will need a car to get here, and remember to bring your own food as there are only picnic areas and no shops.

G. Oakhaven Town
This beautiful historic town is famous for its weekly market, where you can buy unique local crafts and gifts. Learn about the town's past on a free walking tour. It is very cheap to visit and has a direct train link to the city center.

H. The Cosmos Centre
An interactive science and space museum perfect for a rainy day. Explore the planetarium and hands-on exhibits. Located in the city center, it is easily reached by bus or train. It has a great gift shop and cafe, though tickets are expensive.

passages.title: An Interview with Maya Lin
passages.text:
We talked to sixteen-year-old runner Maya Lin about her life on and off the track. Maya recently won the national junior 800-metre championship, but she remains surprisingly down-to-earth.

Interviewer: Maya, congratulations on your gold medal! How did you first get into running?
Maya: Thanks! Actually, it was by accident. When I was eleven, my school's running team was short of one person for a relay race. The coach saw me running to catch the school bus and asked me to fill in. I didn't even have proper running shoes! I ended up running really fast, and the coach suggested I join the club. Before that, I preferred playing video games and reading. I never imagined I would become an athlete.

Interviewer: How do you manage to balance your training with your schoolwork?
Maya: It isn't easy. I train for about two hours every day after school, and more on weekends. I have to be very organized. I do my homework on the bus or during lunch breaks. My friends are very understanding, though they sometimes complain that I can't hang out with them on Friday nights because I have to sleep early for Saturday morning practice. But they always come to support me at my races, which means a lot.

Interviewer: Do you ever feel too much pressure before a big race?
Maya: Definitely. Before a race, my hands shake and I feel sick. But my coach taught me to view that nervous energy as a positive thing. She says it shows my body is preparing to run fast. Once the race starts, all the worry disappears and I just focus on my breathing and my steps. I don't think about winning; I just try to beat my own personal best time.

Interviewer: What are your goals for the future?
Maya: Of course, the Olympics is the ultimate dream, but that is a long way off. For now, I want to focus on my next race and keep improving. I also want to finish my school exams with good grades because education is important to me. If I have one piece of advice for other young people, it's to try new things. You might discover a talent you never knew you had!

passages.title: A Weekend at the Local Food Market

Last Saturday, I decided to visit the local food market in the town centre. I had heard a lot about it from my neighbours, but I had never found the time to go before. [1] As soon as I arrived, I realized I should have come much sooner. The atmosphere was incredibly lively and full of energy.

There were dozens of colourful stalls selling everything from fresh fruit to homemade cakes. [2] The smell of freshly baked bread was particularly amazing, drawing a huge crowd to one corner. I spent about an hour just walking around and looking at all the delicious options.

What I liked most was talking to the people who worked there. [3] They were happy to explain how they made their cheese or where their vegetables were grown. This made the shopping experience feel much more personal than going to a normal supermarket.

By lunchtime, I was starting to feel quite hungry because of all the wonderful smells. [4] I chose a small stall selling traditional Spanish empanadas and sat on a wooden bench to eat them. They were absolutely delicious and very filling.

Before leaving, I bought some fresh pasta and a jar of local honey to take home. [5] I am already planning my next visit and cannot wait to try some of the other stalls.

Last weekend, my family and I went on a trip to the mountains. We decided to go [1] car because it was easier to carry all our bags. The journey took about three hours, and [2] the weather was a bit cloudy at first, it soon became sunny.

When we arrived, we stayed in a lovely wooden cabin [3] was located next to a beautiful lake. My father immediately suggested going for a walk. We walked [4] hours along the forest paths. We even saw some wild deer! Later, my younger brother and I spent the afternoon swimming in the cold, clear water of the lake.

In the evening, we cooked a delicious meal together. Then we all sat outside and looked at the thousands of bright stars above the quiet valley. It was [5] a wonderful experience that we have already decided to return next year. I am really looking forward [6] our next adventure in the mountains.

passages.title: Recording 1: A delayed train
passages.text: Woman: Hi Tom, it's me. I'm still at the station, and I'm afraid I'm going to be late. My train to York was supposed to leave at ten fifteen, but there's a problem with the signals. So I'll probably get to you around lunchtime. Sorry!

passages.text:
Man: So how are you getting to the airport on Friday?
Woman: Well, I was going to take the bus because it's the cheapest, but it takes nearly two hours with all the stops. My brother offered to drive me, but his car's at the garage until next week. So in the end I've booked a seat on the train. It's only forty minutes, and the station is right next to the terminal.
Man: Sounds perfect.
